15	
16	- **Status:** Not Started
17	- **Description:** Make URL-based project context and project membership the authorization boundary for every project-scoped feature. Implement the legacy role model using Project Admin, Project Manager, Reviewer, Validator, and Guest, then replace the legacy global-user dropdown with exact account lookup and secure email invitations.
18	- **Functional Domain:** Project & Protocol Management
19	- **Behavior:** Legacy ReLiS assigns a creator an admin role, then lets project managers and Project Admin add users with one of four visible project roles: Project Manager, Reviewer, Validator, or Guest. Its user-selection UI exposes a dropdown containing all application users. NeoReLiS preserves the functional role model but uses canonical role values, exact lookup, invitation-based onboarding, and auditable project membership.
20	- **Users and permissions:**
21	  - The creator becomes Project Owner when project creation succeeds.
22	  - A Project Admin and Project Manager can add, invite, change the role of, and remove users only within their own project. Note: Project Manager cannot remove a Project Admin.
23	  - A Project Owner/Manager can assign: Project Manager, Reviewer, Validator, or Guest.
24	  - An Application Administrator has audited authority over every application user, invitation, project, and membership.
25	  - Reviewer, Validator, and Guest roles cannot manage project members or invitations.
26	  - A Project Manager has management, review, and validation capabilities; Reviewer and Validator permissions follow the project permission matrix; Guest is read-only access to all public project.
27	  - There is exactly one project role per active membership.
28	- **UI behavior:**
29	  - Provide a Project settings > Team page containing active members and outstanding invitations.
30	  - Show each entry's username, project role, status, added by, added date.
31	  - Do not show a searchable directory, dropdown, autocomplete list, pagination, or bulk export of application users.
32	  - Provide an Add team member form: select the intended project role; enter either an exact username or an exact email address.
33	  - When an exact username matches an existing account, show a confirmation card with its username and registered email, then allow the Project Manager to add that user to the project with the selected role.
34	  - When an exact email matches an existing account, show the matching username, then allow the Project Manager to add that user with the selected role.
35	  - When the username does not match an account, require an email address and keep the selected role.
36	  - The Invite user action performs a final email lookup before sending an invitation. If that email already belongs to an account, do not send an invitation; show the matching-account flow instead. If no account exists, create an invitation and show it with status `Invited`.
37	  - The invitation link expires after the invitation-validity period configured by the Application Administrator — by default it expires after 7 days.
38	  - Project Admin & Managers can resend or cancel an outstanding invitation, change a member's role, or remove a member.
39	  - Role changes and removal must warn about active work assignments. They must never erase prior decisions, assessments, extracted data, or audit history.
40	- **API behavior:**
41	  - Project-context middleware validates the project URL, project state, active membership, and role before executing any project-scoped use case. Application Administrators have audited global access.
42	  - Provide authorized use cases to: list project members and invitations; perform an exact username or email lookup; add an existing account to the current project; create, resend, cancel, and accept an invitation; change a project role; remove or restore a membership.
43	  - Account lookup must: require Project Admin & Manager or Application Administrator profile; accept one exact, normalized username or email value; return only the minimum confirmation information needed for the requested flow; never return a list of users or search suggestions.
44	  - Adding an existing account creates one active project membership after checking: the account exists; the account is not already an active member; the requested role is valid; the action does not violate the last-Project-Manager guard.
45	  - Creating an invitation must: use the normalized email address and selected role; create a `ProjectInvitation` record, not a membership for a non-existent user; generate a single-use, securely random invitation token; store only a hash of the token; expire after 7 days by default if no invitation-validity period was configured by the Application Administrator; invalidate any previous active invitation for the same project and email when resent; send the invitation email asynchronously.
46	  - Accepting an invitation must: validate the token, expiration, invitation status, and email ownership; require registration or sign-in with the invited email address; create one active membership with the invitation's assigned role; mark the invitation `Accepted`; never allow the invitation email or role to be silently changed.
47	- **Data model:**
48	  - Control DB — Global User identity: immutable ID, unique normalized username, unique normalized email, email-verification state, account status, and timestamps.
49	  - Control DB — Project Membership: project ID, user ID, role (`PROJECT_ADMIN`, `PROJECT_MANAGER`, `REVIEWER`, `VALIDATOR`, `GUEST`), status (`ACTIVE`, `REMOVED`), actor, timestamps, and removal reason.
50	  - Control DB — Project Invitation: project ID, normalized email, proposed role, status (`INVITED`, `ACCEPTED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`), token hash, expiration time, inviter, accepted user ID, sent/accepted timestamps.
51	  - Membership and invitation audit events.
52	  - Enforce one active membership per `(projectId, userId)`.
53	  - Enforce at most one active invitation per `(projectId, normalizedEmail)`.
54	  - Project DB: contains no user identities, passwords, invitations, roles, or membership copies.
55	- **Acceptance criteria:**
56	  - [ ] A project-scoped API request is authorized from the URL project ID and active membership.
57	  - [ ] Administrators and Project Admins can manage membership only within their permitted scope.
58	  - [ ] Duplicate active membership is prevented.
59	  - [ ] Guests have read-only access and cannot access mutation endpoints.
60	  - [ ] Removing the last Project Admin is rejected.
61	- **Assigned to:** Empty
62	- **Severity:** Minor
63	- **Blocked by:** Empty
64	- **Jobs behavior:**
65	  - Send invitation and resend emails through the existing transactional email job mechanism.
66	  - Expire invitations after 48 hours through expiry checks and scheduled cleanup; expired invitations cannot be accepted.
67	  - Failed email delivery must be visible to authorized managers without exposing SMTP/provider internals.
68	  - Retries must not create duplicate invitations or send multiple valid tokens unintentionally.
69	- **Audit:**
70	  - exact account lookup; member added; invitation created, sent, resent, cancelled, expired, and accepted; role changed; member removed or restored; rejected duplicate membership, invalid invitation, and last-Project-Manager actions.
71	  - Removing a membership revokes access but never deletes the global account or historic project work. Restoring a removed member is an explicit, audited action.
72	
73	## Objective and summarized requirements
74	
75	Use the URL project and current membership as the authorization boundary, with exact account lookup and secure invitations.
76	
77	## Proposed prerequisites
78	
79	- [03 — Create control Prisma schema](03-control-prisma.md)
80	- [05 — Implement API app shell](05-api-shell.md)
81	- [06 — Complete job queue and progress platform](06-job-platform.md)

83	- [10 — Implement Registration and Email Verification](10-registration.md)

88	
89	1. Define middleware that verifies the URL `projectId`, state, membership, and role; allow audited global support access.
90	2. Implement Team, exact normalized username/email lookup, and adding existing accounts; do not offer a global user directory or autocomplete.
91	3. Implement invitations with a fixed role, random token stored as a hash, expiry, and asynchronous email; check again for an existing account before inviting.
92	4. Accept an invitation only with verified ownership of its email; consume it once and create one active membership.
93	5. Prevent duplicate active memberships and invitations; resending invalidates the previous invitation.
94	6. Implement role changes, removal, and restoration while preserving historical work; show assignment impact and audit actions, including lookup.
95	7. Keep identities, credentials, invitations, memberships, and roles only in the Control DB.
96	
97	## Definition of Done — completion checklist
98	
99	Notion's Acceptance criteria (reproduced above) is the primary source; the items below restate it as concrete, testable points and add detail grounded in the API behavior/Data model/Jobs behavior/Audit fields, which carry unusually rich detail for this card.
100	
101	- [ ] Every project-scoped route resolves authorization from the URL `projectId` + the caller's active membership + role — an ID belonging to a different project can never be used to access data across the boundary.
102	- [ ] `Team` shows active members and outstanding invitations (username, role, status, added-by, added-date) but never a searchable/autocomplete directory of all application users.
103	- [ ] Account lookup accepts only one exact, normalized username or email, returns the minimum confirmation info, and never returns a list/search suggestions.
104	- [ ] Inviting re-checks for an existing account at send time: if the email now matches an account, the invite is not sent and the matching-account flow is shown instead.
105	- [ ] Invitation tokens are single-use, securely random, stored only as a hash, and resending invalidates any previous active invitation for the same `(project, email)` pair.
106	- [ ] Accepting an invitation requires verified ownership of the invited email, creates exactly one active membership with the invitation's role, and marks the invitation `Accepted` — the email or role can never be silently changed during acceptance.
107	- [ ] At most one active membership exists per `(projectId, userId)`, and at most one active invitation per `(projectId, normalizedEmail)` — enforced at the data layer, not just in the UI.
108	- [ ] Guests have read-only access; every mutation endpoint (invite, role change, remove, resend, cancel) rejects Reviewer, Validator, and Guest callers.
109	- [ ] Removing the last Project Admin (or, per the role-cycle decision recorded in [pending decisions](PENDING-DECISIONS.md), the equivalent protected owner role) is rejected; a Project Manager cannot remove a Project Admin.
110	- [ ] Removing a membership revokes access without deleting the global user account or any historical project work/attribution; restoring a removed member is an explicit, audited action.
111	- [ ] Invitation and resend emails are sent asynchronously through the shared job platform ([06](06-job-platform.md)); failed delivery is visible to authorized managers without exposing SMTP/provider internals, and retries do not create duplicate invitations or multiple valid tokens.

  - Adding an existing account creates one active project membership after checking: the account exists; the account is not already an active member; the requested role is valid; the action does not violate the last-Project-Manager guard.
  - Creating an invitation must: use the normalized email address and selected role; create a `ProjectInvitation` record, not a membership for a non-existent user; generate a single-use, securely random invitation token; store only a hash of the token; expire after 7 days by default if no invitation-validity period was configured by the Application Administrator; invalidate any previous active invitation for the same project and email when resent; send the invitation email asynchronously.
  - Accepting an invitation must: validate the token, expiration, invitation status, and email ownership; require registration or sign-in with the invited email address; create one active membership with the invitation's assigned role; mark the invitation `Accepted`; never allow the invitation email or role to be silently changed.
- **Data model:**
  - Control DB — Global User identity: immutable ID, unique normalized username, unique normalized email, email-verification state, account status, and timestamps.
  - Control DB — Project Membership: project ID, user ID, role (`PROJECT_ADMIN`, `PROJECT_MANAGER`, `REVIEWER`, `VALIDATOR`, `GUEST`), status (`ACTIVE`, `REMOVED`), actor, timestamps, and removal reason.
  - Control DB — Project Invitation: project ID, normalized email, proposed role, status (`INVITED`, `ACCEPTED`, `EXPIRED`, `CANCELLED`), token hash, expiration time, inviter, accepted user ID, sent/accepted timestamps.
  - Membership and invitation audit events.
  - Enforce one active membership per `(projectId, userId)`.
  - Enforce at most one active invitation per `(projectId, normalizedEmail)`.
  - Project DB: contains no user identities, passwords, invitations, roles, or membership copies.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - [ ] A project-scoped API request is authorized from the URL project ID and active membership.
  - [ ] Administrators and Project Admins can manage membership only within their permitted scope.
  - [ ] Duplicate active membership is prevented.
  - [ ] Guests have read-only access and cannot access mutation endpoints.
  - [ ] Removing the last Project Admin is rejected.
- **Assigned to:** Empty
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Blocked by:** Empty
- **Jobs behavior:**
  - Send invitation and resend emails through the existing transactional email job mechanism.
  - Expire invitations after 48 hours through expiry checks and scheduled cleanup; expired invitations cannot be accepted.
  - Failed email delivery must be visible to authorized managers without exposing SMTP/provider internals.
  - Retries must not create duplicate invitations or send multiple valid tokens unintentionally.
- **Audit:**
  - exact account lookup; member added; invitation created, sent, resent, cancelled, expired, and accepted; role changed; member removed or restored; rejected duplicate membership, invalid invitation, and last-Project-Manager actions.
  - Removing a membership revokes access but never deletes the global account or historic project work. Restoring a removed member is an explicit, audited action.

## Objective and summarized requirements

Use the URL project and current membership as the authorization boundary, with exact account lookup and secure invitations.

## Step-by-step instructions for the LLM

1. Define middleware that verifies the URL `projectId`, state, membership, and role; allow audited global support access.
2. Implement Team, exact normalized username/email lookup, and adding existing accounts; do not offer a global user directory or autocomplete.
3. Implement invitations with a fixed role, random token stored as a hash, expiry, and asynchronous email; check again for an existing account before inviting.
4. Accept an invitation only with verified ownership of its email; consume it once and create one active membership.
5. Prevent duplicate active memberships and invitations; resending invalidates the previous invitation.
6. Implement role changes, removal, and restoration while preserving historical work; show assignment impact and audit actions, including lookup.
7. Keep identities, credentials, invitations, memberships, and roles only in the Control DB.

## Definition of Done — completion checklist

Notion's Acceptance criteria (reproduced above) is the primary source; the items below restate it as concrete, testable points and add detail grounded in the API behavior/Data model/Jobs behavior/Audit fields, which carry unusually rich detail for this card.

- [ ] Every project-scoped route resolves authorization from the URL `projectId` + the caller's active membership + role — an ID belonging to a different project can never be used to access data across the boundary.
- [ ] `Team` shows active members and outstanding invitations (username, role, status, added-by, added-date) but never a searchable/autocomplete directory of all application users.
- [ ] Account lookup accepts only one exact, normalized username or email, returns the minimum confirmation info, and never returns a list/search suggestions.
- [ ] Inviting re-checks for an existing account at send time: if the email now matches an account, the invite is not sent and the matching-account flow is shown instead.
- [ ] Invitation tokens are single-use, securely random, stored only as a hash, and resending invalidates any previous active invitation for the same `(project, email)` pair.
- [ ] Accepting an invitation requires verified ownership of the invited email, creates exactly one active membership with the invitation's role, and marks the invitation `Accepted` — the email or role can never be silently changed during acceptance.
- [ ] At most one active membership exists per `(projectId, userId)`, and at most one active invitation per `(projectId, normalizedEmail)` — enforced at the data layer, not just in the UI.
- [ ] Guests have read-only access; every mutation endpoint (invite, role change, remove, resend, cancel) rejects Reviewer, Validator, and Guest callers.
- [ ] Removing the last Project Admin (or, per the role-cycle decision recorded in [pending decisions](PENDING-DECISIONS.md), the equivalent protected owner role) is rejected; a Project Manager cannot remove a Project Admin.
- [ ] Removing a membership revokes access without deleting the global user account or any historical project work/attribution; restoring a removed member is an explicit, audited action.
- [ ] Invitation and resend emails are sent asynchronously through the shared job platform ([06](06-job-platform.md)); failed delivery is visible to authorized managers without exposing SMTP/provider internals, and retries do not create duplicate invitations or multiple valid tokens.
- [ ] The resolved invitation-expiry period (7 days per UI/API vs. 48 hours per Jobs behavior — see Gaps) is applied consistently across token generation, UI display, and scheduled cleanup.
- [ ] Every listed action (lookup, member added, invitation lifecycle events, role changed, member removed/restored, and every rejected duplicate/invalid/last-Project-Manager attempt) writes an audit event.
- [ ] All of the above data (identities, credentials, invitations, memberships, roles) lives only in the Control DB — never duplicated into a Project DB.
- [ ] Automated tests cover: cross-project access rejection; duplicate membership/invitation rejection; full invite→accept flow; last-Project-Admin removal rejection; and a Guest's 403 on every mutation endpoint.
- [ ] Report which commands were run and their actual results, and record which invitation-expiry value (7 days vs. 48 hours) and which role model (`PROJECT_ADMIN` vs. protected `PROJECT_OWNER`) were actually chosen, per the decisions required below.

18	- **Functional Domain:** Project & Protocol Management
19	- **Behavior:** Legacy ReLiS imports PHP/editor-generated configuration that controls screening, QA, extraction, and reporting. ReLiS2.0 replaces this with a native structured form. Its validated payload is stored as normalized configuration metadata in the isolated Project DB and interpreted by reusable application code at runtime.
20	- **Users and permissions:**
21	  - Users with project-creation permission can start and submit a project-creation draft.
22	  - Drafts belong to their creator; Application Administrators may access them for support purposes.
23	  - After successful provisioning, the creator becomes Project Owner of the new project.
24	  - Reviewers, Validators, and Guests cannot create or edit project-creation drafts.
25	  - Changes to an active project protocol are out of scope for this ticket and require a future Project Protocol Revisions workflow.
26	  - No frontend user can execute raw SQL, generate database schema, or write directly to Control DB or Project DB tables.
27	- **UI behavior:**
28	  - On the application home page, provide a Create project action with two choices: Create from scratch; Import configuration JSON.
29	  - Create from scratch opens an empty Project Creation Wizard.
30	  - When the user selects Import configuration JSON: display a file-upload dialog for one project-configuration JSON file; show the selected file name and an import-loading state; when the file is valid, open the normal Project Creation Wizard with the imported configuration values prefilled; display a concise import summary and any compatibility warnings at the top of the wizard; allow the user to review and modify every imported field; if the file is invalid or unsupported, show actionable errors and do not open or modify a creation draft; importing a file does not create a project — the user must complete the wizard and explicitly confirm creation.
31	  - Provide a step-based Project Creation Wizard with autosaved drafts, resume/discard actions, per-step validation, a final review screen, and an explicit Create project confirmation. Whether the wizard starts empty or from an imported JSON configuration, it follows the same validation, autosave, review, confirmation, and provisioning flow.
32	
33	  **1. Project identity** — Project title (required); Project short name (required and unique; suggest a value from the title); optional description; optional research questions — ordered, repeatable entries, each with an optional description field.
34	
35	  **2. Modules** — enable/disable switches for: Paper Library & Import; Screening; Screening validation; Quality Assessment; Data Extraction; Reporting / Custom Chart Reports (enabling this also requires Data Extraction).
36	
37	  **3. Import paper** (when Paper Library & Import is enabled) — an optional, repeatable list of paper sources (each with Value — required, Description, Method — required, Search Query); an optional, repeatable list of search strategies (each with its own description); optional label to define a prefix of the paper key.
38	
39	  **3(bis). Screening** (when Screening is enabled) — Reviewers per paper (required, int); Conflict type: decision or criteria (displayed and required when reviewers > 1); Conflict resolution: unanimity or majority (required when reviewers > 1); Exclusion criteria — optional, repeatable (criteria + optional description); Screening inclusion mode (All, one, any, none); Use kappa: yes/no; Inclusion criteria — optional, repeatable (criteria + optional description); Screening phases — at least one required, each with Title, Description, and Fields to display (Title, Abstract, Preview, BibTeX, URL — multiple choice).
40	
41	  **4. Screening validation** (when enabled) — Percentage of excluded papers to validate; Validation outcome handling (Info, Normal, or Veto); Assign papers to validators who have not screened them (yes/no); Screening status to validate (Included, Excluded, Included & excluded).
42	
43	  **5. Quality Assessment** (when enabled) — Ordered QA questions; response label; Minimum total score threshold; optional QA validation settings: enable validation of completed QA assessments (disabled by default), and when enabled, a validation percentage.
44	
45	  **6. Data Extraction** (when enabled) — a category builder. Each category has: Category Type (Simple, List, DynamicList, Dependent DynamicList); Required or optional; Category name (required, unique per project); Label name; Maximum number of selectable values; optional Default value.
46	  - When Simple: Value type (boolean, integer, real, date, string, text); optional validation pattern (RegEx); Maximum text length (optional, default 20); the default-value input adapts to the Value Type.
47	  - When List: list options (at least two distinct values required).
48	  - When DynamicList: optional initial values.
49	  - When Dependent DynamicList: Source DynamicList category (dropdown of existing List categories where possible).
50	  - Every category can contain subcategories via a "+" action.
51	
52	  **7. Custom Chart Report** (when enabled) — Required dimension label: "Simple" (one dimension) or "Compare" (two).
53	  - Simple: chart name (default `chart_name`); category for frequency reporting (dropdown of existing categories); chart_type (Line, Pie, Bar — multi-select).
54	  - Compare: chart name (required, unique); X-axis category; Y-axis category; chart_type (Line, Pie, Bar, Bubble chart — multi-select).
55	
56	  **8. Review and confirmation** — a readable summary of all enabled modules and configured fields; blocking validation errors and concise warnings. After final confirmation, show only creation status: Validating, Provisioning project database, Ready, Failed. On failure, show a human-readable error summary and a safe retry action. Do not show protocol-version comparison, activation, rollback, or change-impact screens in this ticket.
57	
58	- **API behavior:**
59	  - Use Hono only as the HTTP/API layer. Hono validates commands, calls application services, and returns API responses. Hono must not generate Prisma schemas, migrations, SQL, database tables, columns, views, procedures, or per-category structures from protocol input.
60	  - Provide authenticated use cases to: validate an imported JSON configuration; create, retrieve, list, autosave, resume, and discard creation drafts; validate a wizard step or a full project-creation command; submit an idempotent project-creation command; retrieve provisioning status; retry an authorized failed provisioning workflow; export an authorized project's active protocol configuration as portable JSON.
61	  - **JSON configuration import and export** — accept one JSON configuration file through an authenticated endpoint; validate a versioned configuration envelope before processing its content; parse imported JSON as untrusted input only; never interpret imported JSON as SQL, executable code, a Prisma schema, a migration, a database blueprint, a file path, or database connection configuration; normalize a valid imported configuration into the same shared `ProjectCreationDraft` contract used by the wizard; return either validated configuration values suitable for prefilling the wizard, structured field-level errors, unsupported-format-version errors, or non-blocking compatibility warnings; JSON import must not create a Project record, membership, provisioning job, or Project DB; export JSON from the normalized active protocol configuration, never internal database IDs or runtime data.
62	  - **Shared validation contract** — one shared server-side Zod contract for project-creation drafts, imported configurations, step validation, and final submissions; validate only relevant completed fields for a partial draft or step validation, and the entire protocol on final confirmation; return structured field-level errors and non-blocking compatibility warnings in a client-friendly format; final server-side validation remains authoritative, including project-short-name uniqueness (enforced with a Control DB constraint, not only client-side).
63	  - **Drafts** — belong only to their authenticated creator unless an Application Administrator has audited global access; drafts are not projects and must never trigger Project DB provisioning; store each draft's current payload as a JSONB document in the Control DB; use the same versioned JSON contract for draft autosave, draft export, and JSON import.
64	  - **Protocol validation rules** — Screening Validation requires Screening; Custom Chart Reports require Data Extraction and valid referenced extraction categories; Source and Search Strategy tracking require Paper Library & Import; when that tracking is disabled, the corresponding lists must be empty; conflict configuration is required only when reviewers per paper > 1; Paper Source and Search Strategy lists are optional, unique, ordered; the system does not execute searches or connect to declared sources/strategies. Data Extraction/Classification rules use fixed domain models: category names unique within the project; a dependent Dynamic List references an existing Dynamic List category; the backend derives inherited reference names (the client cannot override them); list categories require at least two distinct options; report definitions reference existing eligible extraction configuration keys; category dependencies and reports use portable configuration keys in draft/JSON input, resolved to Project DB records only during protocol persistence; no category/question/phase/source/strategy/report/subcategory ever creates a table, column, Prisma model, migration, SQL statement, view, or procedure.

68	  - **Provisioning retry and status** — make each stage idempotent; a retry after failure reuses an already-cloned Project DB, and does not re-insert configuration rows if `v1` was already persisted; activate the Project and the creator's protected `PROJECT_OWNER` membership only after the Project DB is available and `v1` has been persisted successfully; expose only `validating`/`provisioning`/`ready`/`failed` to the frontend; on failure, return a safe human-readable summary and a retryable/non-retryable status; never return database credentials, connection strings, SQL errors, stack traces, database names, or internal infrastructure details; a retry resumes the same workflow and never creates another Project.
69	- **Data model:**
70	  - Control DB: project-creation drafts, draft owner, current wizard step, autosaved draft payload, project registry, lifecycle/provisioning state, Project DB reference, creator membership, and provisioning-job reference.
71	  - Project DB: immutable initial protocol snapshot (`v1`), module toggles, project settings, screening phases, exclusion criteria, separate project-scoped `PaperSource` and `SearchStrategy` reference records seeded from the initial protocol configuration (imported papers retain nullable references to the selected source/search strategy), QA questions and shared response scale, extraction category definitions, choice-list definitions, category dependencies/subcategories, custom report definitions, and a creation audit record.

# 18 — Build the Native Project Protocol Wizard

## Source and usage

- Source: [Build the Native Project Protocol Wizard](https://app.notion.com/p/Build-the-Native-Project-Protocol-Wizard-3ad4993602938018a7e5d9d1f1da71c4).
- Notion ID: `3ad4993602938018a7e5d9d1f1da71c4`.
- Source domain: Project & Protocol Management.
- Source status on 2026-09-20: Not Started; this does not represent local progress.
- Type: this file reproduces the full Notion card content (all 15 properties, fetched 2026-09-28), plus a locally authored completion checklist. This is the largest and most detailed source card in the set — read it in full before implementing any slice.
- Source `Blocked by` relation: Prepare and Provision an Isolated Project Database Template.

First read the [README](README.md), [pending decisions](PENDING-DECISIONS.md), [stack](../stack.yml), and [required structure](../project-structure.md). Confirm the target repository and existing implementation before editing code. The structure is the required target, not evidence that any feature has been implemented.

## Full Notion card content (fetched 2026-09-28)

- **Status:** Not Started
- **Description:** Replace DSL/Xtext and external-editor project configuration with a native, autosaved React wizard that collects, validates, and creates the complete review protocol. After confirmation, the same feature provisions the isolated Project DB and persists the initial runtime configuration (`v1`).
- **Functional Domain:** Project & Protocol Management
- **Behavior:** Legacy ReLiS imports PHP/editor-generated configuration that controls screening, QA, extraction, and reporting. ReLiS2.0 replaces this with a native structured form. Its validated payload is stored as normalized configuration metadata in the isolated Project DB and interpreted by reusable application code at runtime.
- **Users and permissions:**
  - Users with project-creation permission can start and submit a project-creation draft.
  - Drafts belong to their creator; Application Administrators may access them for support purposes.
  - After successful provisioning, the creator becomes Project Owner of the new project.
  - Reviewers, Validators, and Guests cannot create or edit project-creation drafts.
  - Changes to an active project protocol are out of scope for this ticket and require a future Project Protocol Revisions workflow.
  - No frontend user can execute raw SQL, generate database schema, or write directly to Control DB or Project DB tables.
- **UI behavior:**
  - On the application home page, provide a Create project action with two choices: Create from scratch; Import configuration JSON.
  - Create from scratch opens an empty Project Creation Wizard.
  - When the user selects Import configuration JSON: display a file-upload dialog for one project-configuration JSON file; show the selected file name and an import-loading state; when the file is valid, open the normal Project Creation Wizard with the imported configuration values prefilled; display a concise import summary and any compatibility warnings at the top of the wizard; allow the user to review and modify every imported field; if the file is invalid or unsupported, show actionable errors and do not open or modify a creation draft; importing a file does not create a project — the user must complete the wizard and explicitly confirm creation.
  - Provide a step-based Project Creation Wizard with autosaved drafts, resume/discard actions, per-step validation, a final review screen, and an explicit Create project confirmation. Whether the wizard starts empty or from an imported JSON configuration, it follows the same validation, autosave, review, confirmation, and provisioning flow.

  **1. Project identity** — Project title (required); Project short name (required and unique; suggest a value from the title); optional description; optional research questions — ordered, repeatable entries, each with an optional description field.

  **2. Modules** — enable/disable switches for: Paper Library & Import; Screening; Screening validation; Quality Assessment; Data Extraction; Reporting / Custom Chart Reports (enabling this also requires Data Extraction).

  **3. Import paper** (when Paper Library & Import is enabled) — an optional, repeatable list of paper sources (each with Value — required, Description, Method — required, Search Query); an optional, repeatable list of search strategies (each with its own description); optional label to define a prefix of the paper key.

  **3(bis). Screening** (when Screening is enabled) — Reviewers per paper (required, int); Conflict type: decision or criteria (displayed and required when reviewers > 1); Conflict resolution: unanimity or majority (required when reviewers > 1); Exclusion criteria — optional, repeatable (criteria + optional description); Screening inclusion mode (All, one, any, none); Use kappa: yes/no; Inclusion criteria — optional, repeatable (criteria + optional description); Screening phases — at least one required, each with Title, Description, and Fields to display (Title, Abstract, Preview, BibTeX, URL — multiple choice).

  **4. Screening validation** (when enabled) — Percentage of excluded papers to validate; Validation outcome handling (Info, Normal, or Veto); Assign papers to validators who have not screened them (yes/no); Screening status to validate (Included, Excluded, Included & excluded).

  **5. Quality Assessment** (when enabled) — Ordered QA questions; response label; Minimum total score threshold; optional QA validation settings: enable validation of completed QA assessments (disabled by default), and when enabled, a validation percentage.

  **6. Data Extraction** (when enabled) — a category builder. Each category has: Category Type (Simple, List, DynamicList, Dependent DynamicList); Required or optional; Category name (required, unique per project); Label name; Maximum number of selectable values; optional Default value.
  - When Simple: Value type (boolean, integer, real, date, string, text); optional validation pattern (RegEx); Maximum text length (optional, default 20); the default-value input adapts to the Value Type.
  - When List: list options (at least two distinct values required).
  - When DynamicList: optional initial values.
  - When Dependent DynamicList: Source DynamicList category (dropdown of existing List categories where possible).
  - Every category can contain subcategories via a "+" action.

  **7. Custom Chart Report** (when enabled) — Required dimension label: "Simple" (one dimension) or "Compare" (two).
  - Simple: chart name (default `chart_name`); category for frequency reporting (dropdown of existing categories); chart_type (Line, Pie, Bar — multi-select).
  - Compare: chart name (required, unique); X-axis category; Y-axis category; chart_type (Line, Pie, Bar, Bubble chart — multi-select).

  **8. Review and confirmation** — a readable summary of all enabled modules and configured fields; blocking validation errors and concise warnings. After final confirmation, show only creation status: Validating, Provisioning project database, Ready, Failed. On failure, show a human-readable error summary and a safe retry action. Do not show protocol-version comparison, activation, rollback, or change-impact screens in this ticket.

- **API behavior:**
  - Use Hono only as the HTTP/API layer. Hono validates commands, calls application services, and returns API responses. Hono must not generate Prisma schemas, migrations, SQL, database tables, columns, views, procedures, or per-category structures from protocol input.
  - Provide authenticated use cases to: validate an imported JSON configuration; create, retrieve, list, autosave, resume, and discard creation drafts; validate a wizard step or a full project-creation command; submit an idempotent project-creation command; retrieve provisioning status; retry an authorized failed provisioning workflow; export an authorized project's active protocol configuration as portable JSON.
  - **JSON configuration import and export** — accept one JSON configuration file through an authenticated endpoint; validate a versioned configuration envelope before processing its content; parse imported JSON as untrusted input only; never interpret imported JSON as SQL, executable code, a Prisma schema, a migration, a database blueprint, a file path, or database connection configuration; normalize a valid imported configuration into the same shared `ProjectCreationDraft` contract used by the wizard; return either validated configuration values suitable for prefilling the wizard, structured field-level errors, unsupported-format-version errors, or non-blocking compatibility warnings; JSON import must not create a Project record, membership, provisioning job, or Project DB; export JSON from the normalized active protocol configuration, never internal database IDs or runtime data.
  - **Shared validation contract** — one shared server-side Zod contract for project-creation drafts, imported configurations, step validation, and final submissions; validate only relevant completed fields for a partial draft or step validation, and the entire protocol on final confirmation; return structured field-level errors and non-blocking compatibility warnings in a client-friendly format; final server-side validation remains authoritative, including project-short-name uniqueness (enforced with a Control DB constraint, not only client-side).
  - **Drafts** — belong only to their authenticated creator unless an Application Administrator has audited global access; drafts are not projects and must never trigger Project DB provisioning; store each draft's current payload as a JSONB document in the Control DB; use the same versioned JSON contract for draft autosave, draft export, and JSON import.
  - **Protocol validation rules** — Screening Validation requires Screening; Custom Chart Reports require Data Extraction and valid referenced extraction categories; Source and Search Strategy tracking require Paper Library & Import; when that tracking is disabled, the corresponding lists must be empty; conflict configuration is required only when reviewers per paper > 1; Paper Source and Search Strategy lists are optional, unique, ordered; the system does not execute searches or connect to declared sources/strategies. Data Extraction/Classification rules use fixed domain models: category names unique within the project; a dependent Dynamic List references an existing Dynamic List category; the backend derives inherited reference names (the client cannot override them); list categories require at least two distinct options; report definitions reference existing eligible extraction configuration keys; category dependencies and reports use portable configuration keys in draft/JSON input, resolved to Project DB records only during protocol persistence; no category/question/phase/source/strategy/report/subcategory ever creates a table, column, Prisma model, migration, SQL statement, view, or procedure.
  - **Paper-key generation** — treat the optional paper-key prefix as an immutable `v1` display setting; allow an empty prefix; do not accept a user-managed paper serial/counter; generate any fallback paper reference atomically in the Project DB via a fixed PostgreSQL sequence or counter table already present in `relis_project_template`.
  - **Idempotent project creation** — on final confirmation, accept an idempotent command using an idempotency key; repeated requests with the same key return the existing project/provisioning result; repeated requests must not create duplicate Control DB projects, `PROJECT_OWNER` memberships, provisioning jobs, or Project databases. In one Control DB transaction: create the Project record with state `PROVISIONING`; set `createdByUserId` to the authenticated creator; reserve the unique project short name; create the creator's protected `PROJECT_OWNER` membership with state `PENDING_PROVISIONING`; create one provisioning job/outbox record linked to the Project and idempotency key. `PROJECT_OWNER` is protected backend state: assigned automatically to the creator; cannot be assigned/removed/changed by membership-management endpoints; the backend enforces it corresponds to `Project.createdByUserId`.
  - **Provisioning behavior** — this ticket depends on [16 — Prepare and Provision an Isolated Project Database Template](16-project-template.md); Hono delegates physical database work to a provisioning service/worker; the Control DB transaction and Project DB work form an idempotent provisioning workflow, not one distributed transaction; generate the Project DB identifier from the internal Project UUID, never the title/short name; maintain `relis_project_template` outside the end-user flow; clone it to create the isolated Project DB; verify the clone is reachable and compatible with the running Prisma data model; never run `prisma migrate deploy`, `prisma db push`, generated SQL, or any schema change during creation; never create tables/columns/views/procedures/models/migrations from protocol categories/questions/phases/sources/strategies/classification configuration/report definitions; use Prisma only for normal CRUD against the cloned DB's existing fixed schema; persist initial protocol version `v1` as normalized records (project settings/enabled modules; Paper Sources and Search Strategies; screening configuration/phases/criteria/reviewer/conflict/validation settings; QA questions/options/scoring/threshold; Data Extraction categories/options/dependencies/multi-value definitions/subcategories; Classification categories and subcategories; reporting and Custom Chart Report definitions); an optional canonical JSONB snapshot of `v1` may be retained for audit only, never to drive database creation/structure/authorization.
  - **Provisioning retry and status** — make each stage idempotent; a retry after failure reuses an already-cloned Project DB, and does not re-insert configuration rows if `v1` was already persisted; activate the Project and the creator's protected `PROJECT_OWNER` membership only after the Project DB is available and `v1` has been persisted successfully; expose only `validating`/`provisioning`/`ready`/`failed` to the frontend; on failure, return a safe human-readable summary and a retryable/non-retryable status; never return database credentials, connection strings, SQL errors, stack traces, database names, or internal infrastructure details; a retry resumes the same workflow and never creates another Project.
- **Data model:**
  - Control DB: project-creation drafts, draft owner, current wizard step, autosaved draft payload, project registry, lifecycle/provisioning state, Project DB reference, creator membership, and provisioning-job reference.
  - Project DB: immutable initial protocol snapshot (`v1`), module toggles, project settings, screening phases, exclusion criteria, separate project-scoped `PaperSource` and `SearchStrategy` reference records seeded from the initial protocol configuration (imported papers retain nullable references to the selected source/search strategy), QA questions and shared response scale, extraction category definitions, choice-list definitions, category dependencies/subcategories, custom report definitions, and a creation audit record.
  - Project DB schema uses static Prisma migrations only; configured extraction categories are metadata interpreted at runtime, never dynamically generated columns or tables.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - [ ] A user can create, resume, validate, review, and submit a complete project protocol without DSL/Xtext or ReLiS Editor access.
  - [ ] The wizard covers all legacy project-configuration categories listed in this ticket.
  - [ ] Conditional fields and cross-step validation prevent invalid protocol combinations.
  - [ ] Draft state survives refresh and can be resumed only by its owner or an authorized Application Administrator.
  - [ ] A confirmed valid draft creates exactly one isolated Project DB and one initial protocol configuration version (`v1`).
  - [ ] The initial configuration controls modules, screening settings, QA template, extraction form, and custom report definitions through normalized metadata.
  - [ ] The project creator becomes Project owner only after provisioning succeeds.
  - [ ] No DSL import, generated SQL, generated table, generated view, or stored procedure is used.
  - [ ] Failed provisioning leaves no active project and returns actionable error information.
  - [ ] Repeating the same confirmation request does not create duplicate projects or databases.
- **Assigned to:** Empty
- **Severity:** Empty
- **Blocked by:** Prepare and Provision an Isolated Project Database Template
- **Jobs behavior:** Run Project DB provisioning and initial configuration persistence through an idempotent workflow. Track `validating`, `provisioning`, `ready`, and `failed` states. A failed attempt must never leave an active project pointing to a missing or incomplete Project DB. Retrying the same confirmed draft must safely recover or reuse the same provisioning attempt.
- **Audit:** Empty

## Objective and summarized requirements

Replace the DSL/editor project configuration flow with a native autosaved wizard that validates, creates, and persists the complete v1 protocol, then provisions the isolated Project DB.

16	- **Status:** Not Started
17	- **Description:** Provide a native Project workspace > Settings area where authorized users directly manage the current project settings.
18	- **Functional Domain:** Project & Protocol Management
19	- **Behavior:** Legacy ReLiS lets Project Admin directly edit project settings, Paper Sources, Search Strategies, Screening phases, exclusion criteria, Quality Assessment settings, extraction configuration, and reporting configuration. NeoReLiS preserves these concepts, but uses fixed Prisma models and normal CRUD instead of generated SQL, dynamic tables, views, procedures, or editor-generated configuration.
20	- **Users and permissions:**
21	  - Only `PROJECT_OWNER` can access `/settings` in their own project.
22	  - `PROJECT_OWNER` can add, edit, and delete active protocol settings.
23	  - Application Administrators have audited global access to project protocol settings.
24	  - `REVIEWER`, `VALIDATOR`, and `GUEST` users cannot access or modify Protocol settings.
25	  - `PROJECT_OWNER` remains a protected backend-managed role; this ticket must not allow it to be assigned, changed, or removed.
26	- **UI behavior:**
27	  - Settings entry in project workspace navigation, using the same high-level structure as the Project Creation Wizard, as tabs: General settings; Screening; Quality assessment; Data extraction; Reporting.
28	  - **Access rules** — Project Owner and Application Administrator access every tab; Project Manager can access/manage Screening, Quality assessment, Data extraction, Reporting but must **not** access or modify General settings; Reviewer/Validator/Guest cannot access Settings at all. Backend authorization remains mandatory even when a tab/action is hidden.
29	  - **Direct editing pattern** — use direct editing rather than add/edit dialogs: Add creates a new editable row; Edit turns the row into editable controls (or expands below it for complex config); Save validates and immediately persists; Cancel restores previous values or removes an unsaved new row; Delete uses inline confirmation (Cancel/Delete). Show field-level validation errors next to the control. Show a clear success message after save and a clear integrity error when a change cannot be safely applied. Do not save incomplete/invalid rows. Do not use dialogs except for the Screening phase configuration pop-up.
30	  - **General settings** (Owner/Admin only) — Export project configuration button (downloads current config as JSON). Project details: title, short name (not editable), description — editable. Research questions table (Question | Description | Order | Actions) with move-up/move-down instead of a typed order value.
31	  - **Paper sources** (when Paper Library & Import enabled) — table Source name | Description | Collection method | Original search query | Actions; source name required+unique; collection method required (Automatic/Manual); a source already used by an import/paper is frozen (cannot edit/delete, may be archived).
32	  - **Search strategies** — table Strategy name | Description | Actions; name required+unique; frozen once used, archivable. When Paper Library & Import is disabled, show an empty state + an "Enable" action; confirming enables the module immediately.
33	  - **Screening** (when enabled) — workflow rules section (reviewers per paper, conflict type, conflict resolution, "assign to validators who haven't screened", use kappa, validation percentage, validation outcome handling, screening inclusion mode) shown inline-editable; validation: reviewers per paper required >0; conflict type/resolution required when reviewers>1; validation fields available only when Screening Validation is enabled; show "Not configured" for unset optional values.
34	  - **Screening phases** — table Order | Title | Description | Displayed fields | Configuration type | Final phase | Actions. A phase has title (required), description (optional), paper source (All papers/Previous phase), source paper status (All/Included/Excluded), one+ displayed fields (Title/Abstract/Preview/BibTeX/Link), configuration type (Default/Customised), final phase (Yes/No, unique per project). Backend manages order; UI offers move-up/move-down only, never a manual order field. A phase using "Previous phase" depends on server-managed order; reordering is rejected if it would invalidate started work. Only one active final phase per project.
35	  - **Phase configuration pop-up** (the one allowed dialog) — clicking the Configuration type cell opens it. For Default: show inherited general settings, offer "Customise this phase" (creates a phase-specific config initialized from current general settings). For Customised: editable phase-specific settings (same validation rules as general), offer "Use default configuration" (removes the override, reverts to current general settings) — available even after the phase has started/has assignments/decisions/validation work. Before saving, show a clear impact warning explaining which settings change and that existing assignments/decisions are preserved without automatic deletion/reset/reassignment/reinterpretation.
36	  - **Exclusion criteria** / **Inclusion criteria** — table Criterion | Description | Actions; direct add/edit/inline-confirmed delete. At least one screening phase is required while Screening is enabled. When Screening is disabled, show empty state + enable action.
37	  - **Quality assessment** (when enabled) — rules section (minimum total score threshold, validation enabled, default validation percentage) inline-edit, "Not configured" for unset. Questions table (Question | Actions). Answers table (Answer | Score | Actions) — an answer requires label+score. When disabled, empty state + enable action.
38	  - **Data extraction** (when enabled) — Extraction categories table: Category name | Label | Type | Required | Configuration | Depends on | Subcategories | Actions. Adding creates an editable row; editing/adding a subcategory/complex config expands an inline area below the row. A category has: type (Simple/List/DynamicList/Dependent DynamicList, required); name (required, unique per project); label (optional); required/optional; optional subcategories via "+ Add subcategory" (nested editable row).
39	    - Simple: value type (Boolean/Integer/Real/Date/String/Text); optional validation pattern (RegEx); optional max text length (prefilled 20 for Text, editable/removable); optional default value with input adapted to the value type.
40	    - List: list options (add multiple; at least two distinct required); optional max selectable values (unlimited if unset).
41	    - DynamicList: optional initial values (add multiple); optional max selectable values.
42	    - Dependent DynamicList: source DynamicList category — required, dropdown of eligible existing DynamicList categories; optional max selectable values.
43	    - When disabled, empty state + enable action.
44	  - **Reporting** (when enabled) — standard project statistics generated from workflow data; no configuration controls when nothing is configurable. Custom Chart Reports (when enabled): table Report name | Dimension mode | Category/X-axis | Y-axis | Chart type | Actions; add/edit via inline expandable row. Dimension mode Simple/Compare; chart type Line/Pie/Bar/Bubble chart (for Compare). Simple: one extraction category + one-or-more chart types. Compare: unique report name; X-axis category; Y-axis category; multiple chart types. Only compatible active Data Extraction categories selectable. When Reporting/Custom Chart Reports disabled, empty state + enable action for the required module.
45	  - **Audit metadata and hidden columns** — every persisted settings record stores backend-managed `Created by`, `Created at`, `Modified by`; where displayed in a table, these are hidden columns by default behind a "Show hidden columns" control usable only by Project Owner and Application Administrator (Project Managers cannot reveal them); these values are read-only and backend-authoritative; the client never submits/modifies them.
46	- **API behavior:**
47	  - Hono only as HTTP/API layer: validates commands, calls application services, returns responses; must not generate Prisma schemas/migrations/SQL/tables/columns/views/procedures/per-category structures from settings input.

# Control DB contracts — consolidated requirements inventory

Local sub-issue: [03.02 — Consolidate the Control DB contracts required by
consuming tasks](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-02.md), under
parent [03 — Create control Prisma schema](../../../context/notion-tasks/03-control-prisma.md).

## 0. Purpose and boundaries

This document consolidates, with full traceability, every field, relation,
lifecycle state, and constraint that a local consuming-task guide explicitly
requires for the eight areas this sub-issue covers: **identity, session,
project, membership, invitation, draft, job, audit**. It is an **inspection
and documentation deliverable only**:

- It does **not** define, approve, or implement a Prisma schema. No model,
  field name, or type below is a finalized schema element — each is labeled
  by its evidentiary status (explicit / engineering inference / conflicting
  / unspecified) and traced to the exact guide and field it comes from.
- It does **not** resolve the `PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN` conflict or any
  other contradiction found below — those are recorded as decision gates for
  [03.03](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md) (role/ownership)
  and, where schema-relevant but not role-related, flagged for 03.04 to
  resolve with the user before implementation.
- No implementation code, Prisma schema, migration, generated client, or
  package export was changed to produce this document.

It builds on, and does not duplicate, [`control-database-inventory.md`](control-database-inventory.md)
(sub-issue 03.01's verified baseline: `@relis/database`'s current empty
state, the migration entry point, and existing test coverage) — consult that
document for the current-state package/Prisma/test inventory.

## 1. Scope and source inventory

**Sources read in full for this document** (all local; no Notion, GitHub, or
other external browsing was performed, per this task's instructions):

- [`control-database-inventory.md`](control-database-inventory.md) (03.01 baseline).

- **Conclusion: every field, contract, and relation in §3 below is a future

## 5. Contradictions, missing information, and decision gates

Each item lists the conflicting sources, every affected consumer, the
precise question a decision must answer, and exactly what downstream schema
work it blocks. None of these is resolved by this document; recording them
does not authorize picking a side.

**5.1 — `PROJECT_OWNER` vs. `PROJECT_ADMIN` (role model).** Conflicting
sources: [15 — Data model/Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/15-membership.md)
(five-value role enum headed by `PROJECT_ADMIN`, membership statuses
`ACTIVE`/`REMOVED` only) vs. [18 — Users and permissions/API behavior](../../../context/notion-tasks/18-protocol-wizard.md)
(a protected `PROJECT_OWNER`, a `PENDING_PROVISIONING` status, and a
backend-enforced correspondence to `Project.createdByUserId`); also named in
[21 — Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/21-project-settings.md)
(`PROJECT_OWNER` as the only General-settings-authorized role) and
[PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 22 (audit role-mapping), 23.
Precise question: is `PROJECT_OWNER` (a) an alias asserted over the existing
`PROJECT_ADMIN` value, (b) a distinct, protected sixth role sitting above
`PROJECT_ADMIN`, or (c) the sole protected creator role with `PROJECT_ADMIN`
demoted to an ordinary assignable role? Blocks: the `Membership.role` enum,
the membership-status enum (two vs. more values), and every "last protected
member" guard — all of 03.04's schema work on this table. **Deferred
entirely to [03.03](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md)**, per
this sub-issue's explicit instruction not to finalize role enums here.

**5.2 — Last Project Manager vs. last Project Admin guard.** Conflicting
sources: both **within guide 15 itself** — Acceptance criteria ("Removing
the last Project Admin is rejected") vs. API behavior ("does not violate the
last-Project-Manager guard"); also [PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15 only (but the guard logic is foundational to
membership removal/role-change validation). Precise question: which
role(s) — Manager, Admin, Owner, or more than one independently — trigger a
"cannot remove the last one" rejection? Blocks: membership removal/role-change
validation logic in 03.04; overlaps with 5.1 since the answer likely depends
on how `PROJECT_OWNER` is finally modeled.

**5.3 — Invitation expiry: 7 days vs. 48 hours.** Conflicting sources: 15 —
UI/API behavior (7-day default, admin-configurable) vs. 15 — Jobs behavior
(48 hours); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 3](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15 (token generation, UI display, scheduled cleanup); 23
(if the value is meant to be admin-configurable, its storage key is also
undefined — see §3.5). Precise question: is the default 7 days (configurable)
or a fixed 48 hours, and is it configurable at all? Blocks: `Invitation`'s
expiry default/validation and the scheduled-cleanup job's cutoff logic.

**5.4 — Who may create a project.** Conflicting sources: 19 — Behavior ("any
authenticated user can start a project-creation draft") vs. 18 — Users and
permissions ("users with project-creation permission can start... a draft");
[PENDING-DECISIONS item 6](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 18, 19. Precise question: is draft/project creation open
to every authenticated user, or gated by a permission/role that no source
names explicitly? Blocks: whether `Draft` creation needs an authorization
check against a field that does not yet exist anywhere in this inventory (a
"can-create-projects" flag/role has no source-named representation).

sources: 19 — Gaps (creator-plus-Application-Administrator access alternates
with owner-only editing) and 21 — Gaps (Owner-only per Users/permissions vs.

**5.6 — Direct settings vs. a protocol-revision/activation job (guide 21's
own self-contradiction).** Conflicting sources, all within 21: Description/
most of UI behavior/API behavior/Acceptance-criteria-prose (no
revision/version-comparison/activation/rollback UI) vs. 21 — Jobs behavior
(describes an "idempotent revision job," "persist validation, impact,
progress, and failure reports for the revision," and "duplicate protocol
versions"); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 11](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 21, 23 (which explicitly warns its own labels/settings
revision model "must not reintroduce protocol revisions prohibited in
[21]"). Precise question: does Project Settings ever need any
version/revision/activation data model, or is it strictly direct-editing
with only `createdBy`/`createdAt`/`modifiedBy` columns and no history beyond
that? Blocks: whether any Project DB protocol table needs version/revision
columns at all — directly relevant to this sub-issue's instruction not to
introduce drafts/revisions where a consuming task prohibits them, since 21
prohibits them in its majority text while its own Jobs behavior field
contradicts that.

**5.7 — Project DB connection-mapping storage (missing information, not a
conflict).** No source states this. [17 — Data model](../../../context/notion-tasks/17-project-resolver.md)
is entirely empty ("Data model: Empty"); [16 — Data model](../../../context/notion-tasks/16-project-template.md)
lists provisioning metadata but no explicit "physical database
identifier/connection reference" field, even though 16 — API behavior is
explicit that this value must never be exposed to a client. Affected
consumers: 16, 17. Precise question: where and in what form is the mapping
from `projectId` to its physical, ready Project DB persisted? Blocks: the
resolver's schema cannot be designed in 03.04 without this; recommend
obtaining a decision (or an explicit "to be designed in 03.04 without a
source answer, flagged as an engineering decision") before finalizing the
Control DB project-registry table.

**5.8 — Invitation-validity-period storage location (missing information).**
15 — UI behavior names an Application-Administrator-configured value; 23 —
Data model only describes a generic, keyless "typed global settings"
registry. Affected consumers: 15, 23. Precise question: is this a
`SystemSetting` row (keyed how?), a dedicated Control DB column on some
other table, or a literal constant? Blocks: `Invitation.expirationTime`'s
computation — low severity, since a literal default can stand in once 5.3 is
resolved, but the configurability requirement itself remains unimplemented
until this is answered.

**5.9 — Cross-project audit correlation mechanism (missing information).**
22 — Data model names "cross-project operation correlation metadata" in the
Control DB without defining its shape, while the actual `OperationBatch`/
`CompensatingAction` records live per-project. Affected consumers: 22.
Precise question: what exact Control DB record lets an Application
Administrator search/filter operation history across every Project DB
without fanning out to each one at query time? Blocks: the `AuditEvent`/
correlation schema design in 03.04 — this is a real architectural question,
not merely a field-naming one.

**5.10 — Draft-to-Project conversion disposition (missing information).** No
source (18's Data model/API behavior, or 19) states what happens to a
`Draft` row after its wizard confirmation successfully creates a `Project`.
Affected consumers: 18, 19 (which shows *unfinished* drafts in "My projects"
but never addresses finished ones). Precise question: is the Draft row
deleted, archived, or retained and linked to the resulting Project for
history? Blocks: `Draft` entity lifecycle/retention design in 03.04.

Documenting these ten items does not block the rest of this inventory —
every other field in §3 that is not cited above is unaffected and can
proceed to 03.04 design once 03.03's role decision lands.

## 6. Planned verification scenarios (NOT executed — proposals for 03.04/03.05)

These are derived directly from the constraints recorded in §3 and are
explicitly **not** automated tests, not run, and not evidence of any
behavior today — they are a forward-looking checklist for whoever implements
and tests the eventual schema/repositories.

- **Identity:** duplicate normalized username/email rejected at the data
  layer; archiving the last active Application Administrator rejected;
  archived user cannot authenticate; email-verification token is single-use
  and a second request invalidates the first; password-reset token same;
  Google `ExternalIdentity` lookup by `(provider, sub)` never matches by
  email alone.
- **Session:** a revoked session is rejected even with a non-expired,
  signature-valid token; a password change/reset invalidates every other
  active session for that account, not only the current one.
- **Project:** project short-name uniqueness enforced at the data layer
  (not only client-side); repeating the same provisioning idempotency key
  does not create a second project/database/membership; a non-owner cannot
  mutate project metadata; an archived project rejects writes at the API
  layer.
- **Membership:** at most one active membership per `(projectId, userId)`
  enforced at the data layer; removing the last protected member (per
  whichever role 03.03 settles on) is rejected; a Project Manager cannot
  remove a Project Admin/Owner; removing a membership never deletes the
  underlying User row.
- **Invitation:** at most one active invitation per `(projectId,
  normalizedEmail)` enforced at the data layer; resending invalidates the
  prior token; an expired invitation cannot be accepted; accepting requires
  verified ownership of the invited email and never silently changes the
  stored role.
- **Draft:** a draft is resumable only by its creator or an audited
  Application Administrator; a draft alone never creates a Project DB
  connection or row; final confirmation with a repeated idempotency key
  returns the existing result rather than duplicating anything.
- **Job:** enqueuing the same idempotency key twice does not create a
  second job; `listJobs` never leaks another project's jobs to a Project
  Admin; a job payload never contains a credential-shaped value.
- **Audit:** no code path updates or hard-deletes an `AuditEvent`; a
  control-plane event and a project-resource event for the same logical
  action are both recorded (not merged into one row); a `CompensatingAction`
  preview that said "safe" is re-validated (and can still be rejected) at
  execution time if state changed in between.

## 7. Handoff checklist for 03.03, 03.04, and 03.05

- [ ] **03.03** must resolve §5.1 (`PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN`) and, as
      part of the same decision, should address §5.2 (which role(s) the
      "last protected member" guard protects) since both hinge on the same
      role model. Do not finalize the `Membership.role` or
      `Membership.status` enum before this lands.
- [ ] **03.04** (schema/migrations/client) should treat §3's **explicit**
      rows as the primary input, **inference** rows as needing an explicit
      note in the schema/PR description (not silent adoption), and must
      obtain a decision — or record an explicit, reported engineering
      choice — for every **unspecified**/gap item in §5 before encoding it,
      per this task's "do not silently treat an unresolved requirement as
      settled" instruction. §5.7 (Project DB connection mapping) and §5.9
      (cross-project audit correlation) are the two gaps most likely to
      require real architectural design work, not just a field name.
- [ ] **03.04** must keep the Control DB / Project DB / External boundaries
      in §4 intact: no membership/identity/session data in any Project DB
      (15's explicit negative); no protocol/settings data duplicated into
      the Control DB beyond the specific fields §3.3/§3.6 name (project
      metadata + research-question order only); `AuditEvent` modeled
      separately per database, never as one shared table; pg-boss's own
      tables left alone — only the companion job-metadata model from §3.7
      is this inventory's concern.
- [ ] **03.05** (typed repositories) should expose repository boundaries
      aligned to §3's eight domains rather than one generic data-access
      surface — e.g. a membership repository must not also expose raw
      invitation-token or credential operations, consistent with the parent
      card's "do not expose generic CRUD" requirement.
- [ ] Any schema element introduced in 03.04 that cannot be traced to a row
      in §3, or to a decision recorded in §5, should be treated as scope
      expansion requiring its own justification — this inventory is meant to
      make that check straightforward.

## Acceptance-criteria evidence (for this sub-issue, 03.02)

- **Every listed field/relation has a source or an explicit inference/decision
  label:** every row in §3's eight tables carries a Status column value
  (explicit / inference / conflicting / unspecified) and a Source column
  citing the exact guide and section it was reproduced from.
- **All eight requested domains are accounted for, including explicit
  "unspecified" findings:** §3.1–§3.8 cover identity, session, project,
  membership, invitation, draft, job, and audit in order; each contains at
  least one row explicitly labeled "unspecified" or flagged as a gap where
  the sources leave a representation undefined (e.g. §3.1's account-status
  enum, §3.3's connection-mapping gap, §3.6's draft-disposition gap, §3.8's
  correlation-mechanism gap).
- **Undefined role and ownership semantics are flagged before constraints
  are proposed:** §5.1/§5.2 record the `PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN` and
  last-protected-member conflicts without proposing a resolution, and §3.4's
  role-enum row is explicitly marked "conflicting" rather than defaulting to
  either source's version.
- **No business schema or repository implementation is introduced:** this
  document contains no Prisma syntax, no TypeScript interface, and no code
  change; §2 confirms `@relis/contracts` and `@relis/database` are unchanged
  from the 03.01 baseline.
- **No unresolved requirement is silently treated as settled:** §5's ten

Local sub-issue: [03.02 — Consolidate the Control DB contracts required by
consuming tasks](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-02.md), under
parent [03 — Create control Prisma schema](../../../context/notion-tasks/03-control-prisma.md).

## 0. Purpose and boundaries

This document consolidates, with full traceability, every field, relation,
lifecycle state, and constraint that a local consuming-task guide explicitly
requires for the eight areas this sub-issue covers: **identity, session,
project, membership, invitation, draft, job, audit**. It is an **inspection
and documentation deliverable only**:

- It does **not** define, approve, or implement a Prisma schema. No model,
  field name, or type below is a finalized schema element — each is labeled
  by its evidentiary status (explicit / engineering inference / conflicting
  / unspecified) and traced to the exact guide and field it comes from.
- It does **not** resolve the `PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN` conflict or any
  other contradiction found below — those are recorded as decision gates for
  [03.03](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md) (role/ownership)
  and, where schema-relevant but not role-related, flagged for 03.04 to
  resolve with the user before implementation.
- No implementation code, Prisma schema, migration, generated client, or
  package export was changed to produce this document.

It builds on, and does not duplicate, [`control-database-inventory.md`](control-database-inventory.md)
(sub-issue 03.01's verified baseline: `@relis/database`'s current empty
state, the migration entry point, and existing test coverage) — consult that
document for the current-state package/Prisma/test inventory.

## 5. Contradictions, missing information, and decision gates

Each item lists the conflicting sources, every affected consumer, the
precise question a decision must answer, and exactly what downstream schema
work it blocks. None of these is resolved by this document; recording them
