**5.1 — `PROJECT_OWNER` vs. `PROJECT_ADMIN` (role model).** Conflicting
sources: [15 — Data model/Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/15-membership.md)
(five-value role enum headed by `PROJECT_ADMIN`, membership statuses
`ACTIVE`/`REMOVED` only) vs. [18 — Users and permissions/API behavior](../../../context/notion-tasks/18-protocol-wizard.md)
(a protected `PROJECT_OWNER`, a `PENDING_PROVISIONING` status, and a
backend-enforced correspondence to `Project.createdByUserId`); also named in
[21 — Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/21-project-settings.md)
(`PROJECT_OWNER` as the only General-settings-authorized role) and
[PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 22 (audit role-mapping), 23.
Precise question: is `PROJECT_OWNER` (a) an alias asserted over the existing
`PROJECT_ADMIN` value, (b) a distinct, protected sixth role sitting above
`PROJECT_ADMIN`, or (c) the sole protected creator role with `PROJECT_ADMIN`
demoted to an ordinary assignable role? Blocks: the `Membership.role` enum,
the membership-status enum (two vs. more values), and every "last protected
member" guard — all of 03.04's schema work on this table. **Deferred
entirely to [03.03](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md)**, per
this sub-issue's explicit instruction not to finalize role enums here.

**5.2 — Last Project Manager vs. last Project Admin guard.** Conflicting
sources: both **within guide 15 itself** — Acceptance criteria ("Removing
the last Project Admin is rejected") vs. API behavior ("does not violate the
last-Project-Manager guard"); also [PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15 only (but the guard logic is foundational to
membership removal/role-change validation). Precise question: which
role(s) — Manager, Admin, Owner, or more than one independently — trigger a
"cannot remove the last one" rejection? Blocks: membership removal/role-change
validation logic in 03.04; overlaps with 5.1 since the answer likely depends
on how `PROJECT_OWNER` is finally modeled.

**5.3 — Invitation expiry: 7 days vs. 48 hours.** Conflicting sources: 15 —
UI/API behavior (7-day default, admin-configurable) vs. 15 — Jobs behavior
(48 hours); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 3](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15 (token generation, UI display, scheduled cleanup); 23
(if the value is meant to be admin-configurable, its storage key is also
undefined — see §3.5). Precise question: is the default 7 days (configurable)
or a fixed 48 hours, and is it configurable at all? Blocks: `Invitation`'s
expiry default/validation and the scheduled-cleanup job's cutoff logic.

**5.4 — Who may create a project.** Conflicting sources: 19 — Behavior ("any
authenticated user can start a project-creation draft") vs. 18 — Users and
permissions ("users with project-creation permission can start... a draft");
[PENDING-DECISIONS item 6](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 18, 19. Precise question: is draft/project creation open
to every authenticated user, or gated by a permission/role that no source
names explicitly? Blocks: whether `Draft` creation needs an authorization
check against a field that does not yet exist anywhere in this inventory (a
"can-create-projects" flag/role has no source-named representation).

**5.5 — Project ownership/administration access matrix.** Conflicting
sources: 19 — Gaps (creator-plus-Application-Administrator access alternates
with owner-only editing) and 21 — Gaps (Owner-only per Users/permissions vs.
Project-Manager-inclusive per UI behavior's "Access rules"); [PENDING-DECISIONS
items 6 and 11](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md). Affected
consumers: 19, 21. Precise question: the exact per-action/per-tab
authorization matrix for Owner/Manager/Admin. Blocks: mostly an
authorization-layer decision, not a schema field — but it determines whether
any "settings access grant" needs its own schema representation at all
(current reading: no — authorization is role-derived, not a separate grant
table — but this is itself only an inference pending the decision).

**5.6 — Direct settings vs. a protocol-revision/activation job (guide 21's
own self-contradiction).** Conflicting sources, all within 21: Description/
most of UI behavior/API behavior/Acceptance-criteria-prose (no
revision/version-comparison/activation/rollback UI) vs. 21 — Jobs behavior
(describes an "idempotent revision job," "persist validation, impact,
progress, and failure reports for the revision," and "duplicate protocol
versions"); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 11](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 21, 23 (which explicitly warns its own labels/settings
revision model "must not reintroduce protocol revisions prohibited in
[21]"). Precise question: does Project Settings ever need any
version/revision/activation data model, or is it strictly direct-editing
with only `createdBy`/`createdAt`/`modifiedBy` columns and no history beyond
that? Blocks: whether any Project DB protocol table needs version/revision
columns at all — directly relevant to this sub-issue's instruction not to
introduce drafts/revisions where a consuming task prohibits them, since 21
prohibits them in its majority text while its own Jobs behavior field
contradicts that.

**5.7 — Project DB connection-mapping storage (missing information, not a
conflict).** No source states this. [17 — Data model](../../../context/notion-tasks/17-project-resolver.md)
is entirely empty ("Data model: Empty"); [16 — Data model](../../../context/notion-tasks/16-project-template.md)
lists provisioning metadata but no explicit "physical database
identifier/connection reference" field, even though 16 — API behavior is
explicit that this value must never be exposed to a client. Affected
consumers: 16, 17. Precise question: where and in what form is the mapping
from `projectId` to its physical, ready Project DB persisted? Blocks: the
resolver's schema cannot be designed in 03.04 without this; recommend
obtaining a decision (or an explicit "to be designed in 03.04 without a
source answer, flagged as an engineering decision") before finalizing the
Control DB project-registry table.

**5.8 — Invitation-validity-period storage location (missing information).**
15 — UI behavior names an Application-Administrator-configured value; 23 —
Data model only describes a generic, keyless "typed global settings"
registry. Affected consumers: 15, 23. Precise question: is this a
`SystemSetting` row (keyed how?), a dedicated Control DB column on some
other table, or a literal constant? Blocks: `Invitation.expirationTime`'s
computation — low severity, since a literal default can stand in once 5.3 is
resolved, but the configurability requirement itself remains unimplemented
until this is answered.

**5.9 — Cross-project audit correlation mechanism (missing information).**
22 — Data model names "cross-project operation correlation metadata" in the
Control DB without defining its shape, while the actual `OperationBatch`/
`CompensatingAction` records live per-project. Affected consumers: 22.

not merely a field-naming one.

source (18's Data model/API behavior, or 19) states what happens to a
`Draft` row after its wizard confirmation successfully creates a `Project`.
Affected consumers: 18, 19 (which shows *unfinished* drafts in "My projects"
but never addresses finished ones). Precise question: is the Draft row
deleted, archived, or retained and linked to the resulting Project for
history? Blocks: `Draft` entity lifecycle/retention design in 03.04.

Documenting these ten items does not block the rest of this inventory —
every other field in §3 that is not cited above is unaffected and can
proceed to 03.04 design once 03.03's role decision lands.

## 6. Planned verification scenarios (NOT executed — proposals for 03.04/03.05)

These are derived directly from the constraints recorded in §3 and are
explicitly **not** automated tests, not run, and not evidence of any
behavior today — they are a forward-looking checklist for whoever implements
and tests the eventual schema/repositories.

- **Identity:** duplicate normalized username/email rejected at the data
  layer; archiving the last active Application Administrator rejected;
  archived user cannot authenticate; email-verification token is single-use
  and a second request invalidates the first; password-reset token same;
  Google `ExternalIdentity` lookup by `(provider, sub)` never matches by
  email alone.
- **Session:** a revoked session is rejected even with a non-expired,
  signature-valid token; a password change/reset invalidates every other
  active session for that account, not only the current one.
- **Project:** project short-name uniqueness enforced at the data layer
  (not only client-side); repeating the same provisioning idempotency key
  does not create a second project/database/membership; a non-owner cannot
  mutate project metadata; an archived project rejects writes at the API
  layer.
- **Membership:** at most one active membership per `(projectId, userId)`
  enforced at the data layer; removing the last protected member (per
  whichever role 03.03 settles on) is rejected; a Project Manager cannot
  remove a Project Admin/Owner; removing a membership never deletes the
  underlying User row.
- **Invitation:** at most one active invitation per `(projectId,
  normalizedEmail)` enforced at the data layer; resending invalidates the
  prior token; an expired invitation cannot be accepted; accepting requires
  verified ownership of the invited email and never silently changes the
  stored role.
- **Draft:** a draft is resumable only by its creator or an audited
  Application Administrator; a draft alone never creates a Project DB
  connection or row; final confirmation with a repeated idempotency key
  returns the existing result rather than duplicating anything.
- **Job:** enqueuing the same idempotency key twice does not create a
  second job; `listJobs` never leaks another project's jobs to a Project
  Admin; a job payload never contains a credential-shaped value.
- **Audit:** no code path updates or hard-deletes an `AuditEvent`; a
  control-plane event and a project-resource event for the same logical
  action are both recorded (not merged into one row); a `CompensatingAction`
  preview that said "safe" is re-validated (and can still be rejected) at
  execution time if state changed in between.

## 7. Handoff checklist for 03.03, 03.04, and 03.05

- [ ] **03.03** must resolve §5.1 (`PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN`) and, as
      part of the same decision, should address §5.2 (which role(s) the
      "last protected member" guard protects) since both hinge on the same
      role model. Do not finalize the `Membership.role` or
      `Membership.status` enum before this lands.
- [ ] **03.04** (schema/migrations/client) should treat §3's **explicit**
      rows as the primary input, **inference** rows as needing an explicit
      note in the schema/PR description (not silent adoption), and must
      obtain a decision — or record an explicit, reported engineering
      choice — for every **unspecified**/gap item in §5 before encoding it,
      per this task's "do not silently treat an unresolved requirement as
      settled" instruction. §5.7 (Project DB connection mapping) and §5.9
      (cross-project audit correlation) are the two gaps most likely to
      require real architectural design work, not just a field name.
- [ ] **03.04** must keep the Control DB / Project DB / External boundaries
      in §4 intact: no membership/identity/session data in any Project DB
      (15's explicit negative); no protocol/settings data duplicated into
      the Control DB beyond the specific fields §3.3/§3.6 name (project
      metadata + research-question order only); `AuditEvent` modeled
      separately per database, never as one shared table; pg-boss's own
      tables left alone — only the companion job-metadata model from §3.7
      is this inventory's concern.
- [ ] **03.05** (typed repositories) should expose repository boundaries
      aligned to §3's eight domains rather than one generic data-access
      surface — e.g. a membership repository must not also expose raw
      invitation-token or credential operations, consistent with the parent
      card's "do not expose generic CRUD" requirement.
- [ ] Any schema element introduced in 03.04 that cannot be traced to a row
      in §3, or to a decision recorded in §5, should be treated as scope
      expansion requiring its own justification — this inventory is meant to
      make that check straightforward.

## Acceptance-criteria evidence (for this sub-issue, 03.02)

- **Every listed field/relation has a source or an explicit inference/decision
  label:** every row in §3's eight tables carries a Status column value
  (explicit / inference / conflicting / unspecified) and a Source column
  citing the exact guide and section it was reproduced from.
- **All eight requested domains are accounted for, including explicit
  "unspecified" findings:** §3.1–§3.8 cover identity, session, project,
  membership, invitation, draft, job, and audit in order; each contains at
  least one row explicitly labeled "unspecified" or flagged as a gap where
  the sources leave a representation undefined (e.g. §3.1's account-status
  enum, §3.3's connection-mapping gap, §3.6's draft-disposition gap, §3.8's
  correlation-mechanism gap).
- **Undefined role and ownership semantics are flagged before constraints
  are proposed:** §5.1/§5.2 record the `PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN` and
  last-protected-member conflicts without proposing a resolution, and §3.4's
  role-enum row is explicitly marked "conflicting" rather than defaulting to
  either source's version.
- **No business schema or repository implementation is introduced:** this
  document contains no Prisma syntax, no TypeScript interface, and no code
  change; §2 confirms `@relis/contracts` and `@relis/database` are unchanged
  from the 03.01 baseline.
- **No unresolved requirement is silently treated as settled:** §5's ten
  items are each phrased as an open question with affected consumers and
  blocked downstream work, not as a chosen interpretation; §6's scenarios
  are explicitly labeled "NOT executed."

## 2. Implemented contracts vs. future requirements

- **`@relis/contracts`** ([`package.json`](../../packages/contracts/package.json),
  [`src/index.ts`](../../packages/contracts/src/index.ts)) exists and is
  workspace-registered, but its entire source is `export { z } from "zod";`
  — it re-exports the Zod library itself and defines **zero** domain
  schemas. A repository-wide search for `@relis/contracts` as an imported
  specifier found no consumers anywhere in `apps/*` or `packages/*` — nothing
  currently imports it.
- **`@relis/database`**: per the 03.01 baseline, `index.ts` is `export {};`
  and both Prisma schemas are model-free (see that document's §2–§3 for full
  detail; not repeated here).
- **Conclusion: every field, contract, and relation in §3 below is a future
  requirement.** Nothing in this inventory has an implemented counterpart in
  this checkout today. This document does not change that — it is the input
  03.04/03.05 will design against.

Each item lists the conflicting sources, every affected consumer, the
precise question a decision must answer, and exactly what downstream schema
work it blocks. None of these is resolved by this document; recording them
does not authorize picking a side.

**5.1 — `PROJECT_OWNER` vs. `PROJECT_ADMIN` (role model).** Conflicting
sources: [15 — Data model/Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/15-membership.md)
(five-value role enum headed by `PROJECT_ADMIN`, membership statuses
`ACTIVE`/`REMOVED` only) vs. [18 — Users and permissions/API behavior](../../../context/notion-tasks/18-protocol-wizard.md)
(a protected `PROJECT_OWNER`, a `PENDING_PROVISIONING` status, and a
backend-enforced correspondence to `Project.createdByUserId`); also named in
[21 — Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/21-project-settings.md)
(`PROJECT_OWNER` as the only General-settings-authorized role) and
[PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 22 (audit role-mapping), 23.
Precise question: is `PROJECT_OWNER` (a) an alias asserted over the existing
`PROJECT_ADMIN` value, (b) a distinct, protected sixth role sitting above
`PROJECT_ADMIN`, or (c) the sole protected creator role with `PROJECT_ADMIN`
demoted to an ordinary assignable role? Blocks: the `Membership.role` enum,
the membership-status enum (two vs. more values), and every "last protected
member" guard — all of 03.04's schema work on this table. **Deferred
entirely to [03.03](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md)**, per
this sub-issue's explicit instruction not to finalize role enums here.

sources: both **within guide 15 itself** — Acceptance criteria ("Removing
the last Project Admin is rejected") vs. API behavior ("does not violate the
last-Project-Manager guard"); also [PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15 only (but the guard logic is foundational to
membership removal/role-change validation). Precise question: which
role(s) — Manager, Admin, Owner, or more than one independently — trigger a
"cannot remove the last one" rejection? Blocks: membership removal/role-change
validation logic in 03.04; overlaps with 5.1 since the answer likely depends
on how `PROJECT_OWNER` is finally modeled.

**5.3 — Invitation expiry: 7 days vs. 48 hours.** Conflicting sources: 15 —
UI/API behavior (7-day default, admin-configurable) vs. 15 — Jobs behavior
(48 hours); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 3](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15 (token generation, UI display, scheduled cleanup); 23
(if the value is meant to be admin-configurable, its storage key is also
undefined — see §3.5). Precise question: is the default 7 days (configurable)
or a fixed 48 hours, and is it configurable at all? Blocks: `Invitation`'s
expiry default/validation and the scheduled-cleanup job's cutoff logic.

**5.4 — Who may create a project.** Conflicting sources: 19 — Behavior ("any
authenticated user can start a project-creation draft") vs. 18 — Users and
permissions ("users with project-creation permission can start... a draft");
[PENDING-DECISIONS item 6](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 18, 19. Precise question: is draft/project creation open
to every authenticated user, or gated by a permission/role that no source
names explicitly? Blocks: whether `Draft` creation needs an authorization
check against a field that does not yet exist anywhere in this inventory (a
"can-create-projects" flag/role has no source-named representation).

**5.5 — Project ownership/administration access matrix.** Conflicting
sources: 19 — Gaps (creator-plus-Application-Administrator access alternates
with owner-only editing) and 21 — Gaps (Owner-only per Users/permissions vs.
Project-Manager-inclusive per UI behavior's "Access rules"); [PENDING-DECISIONS
items 6 and 11](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md). Affected
consumers: 19, 21. Precise question: the exact per-action/per-tab
authorization matrix for Owner/Manager/Admin. Blocks: mostly an
authorization-layer decision, not a schema field — but it determines whether
any "settings access grant" needs its own schema representation at all
(current reading: no — authorization is role-derived, not a separate grant
table — but this is itself only an inference pending the decision).

**5.6 — Direct settings vs. a protocol-revision/activation job (guide 21's
own self-contradiction).** Conflicting sources, all within 21: Description/
most of UI behavior/API behavior/Acceptance-criteria-prose (no
revision/version-comparison/activation/rollback UI) vs. 21 — Jobs behavior
(describes an "idempotent revision job," "persist validation, impact,
progress, and failure reports for the revision," and "duplicate protocol
versions"); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 11](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 21, 23 (which explicitly warns its own labels/settings
revision model "must not reintroduce protocol revisions prohibited in
[21]"). Precise question: does Project Settings ever need any
version/revision/activation data model, or is it strictly direct-editing
with only `createdBy`/`createdAt`/`modifiedBy` columns and no history beyond
that? Blocks: whether any Project DB protocol table needs version/revision
columns at all — directly relevant to this sub-issue's instruction not to
introduce drafts/revisions where a consuming task prohibits them, since 21
prohibits them in its majority text while its own Jobs behavior field
contradicts that.

**5.7 — Project DB connection-mapping storage (missing information, not a
conflict).** No source states this. [17 — Data model](../../../context/notion-tasks/17-project-resolver.md)
is entirely empty ("Data model: Empty"); [16 — Data model](../../../context/notion-tasks/16-project-template.md)
lists provisioning metadata but no explicit "physical database
identifier/connection reference" field, even though 16 — API behavior is
explicit that this value must never be exposed to a client. Affected
consumers: 16, 17. Precise question: where and in what form is the mapping
from `projectId` to its physical, ready Project DB persisted? Blocks: the
resolver's schema cannot be designed in 03.04 without this; recommend
obtaining a decision (or an explicit "to be designed in 03.04 without a
source answer, flagged as an engineering decision") before finalizing the
Control DB project-registry table.

**5.8 — Invitation-validity-period storage location (missing information).**
15 — UI behavior names an Application-Administrator-configured value; 23 —
Data model only describes a generic, keyless "typed global settings"
registry. Affected consumers: 15, 23. Precise question: is this a
`SystemSetting` row (keyed how?), a dedicated Control DB column on some
other table, or a literal constant? Blocks: `Invitation.expirationTime`'s
computation — low severity, since a literal default can stand in once 5.3 is
resolved, but the configurability requirement itself remains unimplemented
until this is answered.

**5.9 — Cross-project audit correlation mechanism (missing information).**
22 — Data model names "cross-project operation correlation metadata" in the
Control DB without defining its shape, while the actual `OperationBatch`/
`CompensatingAction` records live per-project. Affected consumers: 22.
Precise question: what exact Control DB record lets an Application
Administrator search/filter operation history across every Project DB
without fanning out to each one at query time? Blocks: the `AuditEvent`/
correlation schema design in 03.04 — this is a real architectural question,
not merely a field-naming one.

**5.10 — Draft-to-Project conversion disposition (missing information).** No
source (18's Data model/API behavior, or 19) states what happens to a
`Draft` row after its wizard confirmation successfully creates a `Project`.
Affected consumers: 18, 19 (which shows *unfinished* drafts in "My projects"
but never addresses finished ones). Precise question: is the Draft row
deleted, archived, or retained and linked to the resulting Project for
history? Blocks: `Draft` entity lifecycle/retention design in 03.04.

Documenting these ten items does not block the rest of this inventory —
every other field in §3 that is not cited above is unaffected and can
proceed to 03.04 design once 03.03's role decision lands.

## 6. Planned verification scenarios (NOT executed — proposals for 03.04/03.05)

These are derived directly from the constraints recorded in §3 and are
explicitly **not** automated tests, not run, and not evidence of any
behavior today — they are a forward-looking checklist for whoever implements
and tests the eventual schema/repositories.

- **Identity:** duplicate normalized username/email rejected at the data
  layer; archiving the last active Application Administrator rejected;
  archived user cannot authenticate; email-verification token is single-use
  and a second request invalidates the first; password-reset token same;
  Google `ExternalIdentity` lookup by `(provider, sub)` never matches by
  email alone.
- **Session:** a revoked session is rejected even with a non-expired,
  signature-valid token; a password change/reset invalidates every other
  active session for that account, not only the current one.
- **Project:** project short-name uniqueness enforced at the data layer
  (not only client-side); repeating the same provisioning idempotency key
  does not create a second project/database/membership; a non-owner cannot
  mutate project metadata; an archived project rejects writes at the API
  layer.
- **Membership:** at most one active membership per `(projectId, userId)`
  enforced at the data layer; removing the last protected member (per
  whichever role 03.03 settles on) is rejected; a Project Manager cannot
  remove a Project Admin/Owner; removing a membership never deletes the
  underlying User row.
- **Invitation:** at most one active invitation per `(projectId,
  normalizedEmail)` enforced at the data layer; resending invalidates the
  prior token; an expired invitation cannot be accepted; accepting requires
  verified ownership of the invited email and never silently changes the
  stored role.
- **Draft:** a draft is resumable only by its creator or an audited
  Application Administrator; a draft alone never creates a Project DB
  connection or row; final confirmation with a repeated idempotency key
  returns the existing result rather than duplicating anything.
- **Job:** enqueuing the same idempotency key twice does not create a
  second job; `listJobs` never leaks another project's jobs to a Project
  Admin; a job payload never contains a credential-shaped value.
- **Audit:** no code path updates or hard-deletes an `AuditEvent`; a
  control-plane event and a project-resource event for the same logical
  action are both recorded (not merged into one row); a `CompensatingAction`
  preview that said "safe" is re-validated (and can still be rejected) at
  execution time if state changed in between.

## 7. Handoff checklist for 03.03, 03.04, and 03.05

- [ ] **03.03** must resolve §5.1 (`PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN`) and, as
      part of the same decision, should address §5.2 (which role(s) the
      "last protected member" guard protects) since both hinge on the same
      role model. Do not finalize the `Membership.role` or
      `Membership.status` enum before this lands.
- [ ] **03.04** (schema/migrations/client) should treat §3's **explicit**
      rows as the primary input, **inference** rows as needing an explicit
      note in the schema/PR description (not silent adoption), and must
      obtain a decision — or record an explicit, reported engineering
      choice — for every **unspecified**/gap item in §5 before encoding it,
      per this task's "do not silently treat an unresolved requirement as
      settled" instruction. §5.7 (Project DB connection mapping) and §5.9
      (cross-project audit correlation) are the two gaps most likely to
      require real architectural design work, not just a field name.
- [ ] **03.04** must keep the Control DB / Project DB / External boundaries
      in §4 intact: no membership/identity/session data in any Project DB
      (15's explicit negative); no protocol/settings data duplicated into
      the Control DB beyond the specific fields §3.3/§3.6 name (project
      metadata + research-question order only); `AuditEvent` modeled
      separately per database, never as one shared table; pg-boss's own
      tables left alone — only the companion job-metadata model from §3.7
      is this inventory's concern.
- [ ] **03.05** (typed repositories) should expose repository boundaries
      aligned to §3's eight domains rather than one generic data-access
      surface — e.g. a membership repository must not also expose raw
      invitation-token or credential operations, consistent with the parent
      card's "do not expose generic CRUD" requirement.
- [ ] Any schema element introduced in 03.04 that cannot be traced to a row
      in §3, or to a decision recorded in §5, should be treated as scope
      expansion requiring its own justification — this inventory is meant to
      make that check straightforward.

## Acceptance-criteria evidence (for this sub-issue, 03.02)

- **Every listed field/relation has a source or an explicit inference/decision
  label:** every row in §3's eight tables carries a Status column value
  (explicit / inference / conflicting / unspecified) and a Source column
  citing the exact guide and section it was reproduced from.
- **All eight requested domains are accounted for, including explicit
  "unspecified" findings:** §3.1–§3.8 cover identity, session, project,
  membership, invitation, draft, job, and audit in order; each contains at
  least one row explicitly labeled "unspecified" or flagged as a gap where
  the sources leave a representation undefined (e.g. §3.1's account-status
  enum, §3.3's connection-mapping gap, §3.6's draft-disposition gap, §3.8's
  correlation-mechanism gap).
- **Undefined role and ownership semantics are flagged before constraints
  are proposed:** §5.1/§5.2 record the `PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN` and
  last-protected-member conflicts without proposing a resolution, and §3.4's
  role-enum row is explicitly marked "conflicting" rather than defaulting to
  either source's version.
- **No business schema or repository implementation is introduced:** this
  document contains no Prisma syntax, no TypeScript interface, and no code
  change; §2 confirms `@relis/contracts` and `@relis/database` are unchanged
  from the 03.01 baseline.
- **No unresolved requirement is silently treated as settled:** §5's ten
  items are each phrased as an open question with affected consumers and
  blocked downstream work, not as a chosen interpretation; §6's scenarios
  are explicitly labeled "NOT executed."

1	# 39 — Implement CSV and BibTeX Reporting Exports
2	
3	## Source and usage
4	
5	- Source: [Implement CSV and BibTeX Reporting Exports](https://app.notion.com/p/Implement-CSV-and-BibTeX-Reporting-Exports-3b349936029380cd93b2d6447bdbbce0).
6	- Notion ID: `3b349936029380cd93b2d6447bdbbce0`.
7	- Source domain: Reporting & Export.
8	- Source status on 2026-09-20: Backlog; this does not represent local progress.
9	- Type: this file reproduces the full Notion card content (all 15 properties, fetched 2026-09-28), plus a locally authored completion checklist.
10	- Source `Blocked by` relation: Empty.
11	
12	First read the [README](README.md), [pending decisions](PENDING-DECISIONS.md), [stack](../stack.yml), and [required structure](../project-structure.md). Confirm the target repository and existing implementation before editing code. The structure is the required target, not evidence that any feature has been implemented.
13	
14	## Full Notion card content (fetched 2026-09-28)
15	
16	- **Status:** Backlog
17	- **Description:** Provide direct project-scoped CSV and BibTeX exports from the Reporting area. The new relis keeps the export scopes provided by legacy ReLiS, but generates the requested file from the current Project DB and downloads it immediately. Generated files are not stored, reused, or made available through predictable server paths.
18	- **Functional Domain:** Reporting & Export
19	- **Behavior:** Legacy ReLiS provides: a CSV export of all active Papers; a CSV export of Papers excluded during Screening; a CSV export of Papers excluded during Classification/Data Extraction; a CSV export of completed Classification/Data Extraction results; BibTeX exports for all, included, and excluded Papers. The new relis keeps these export scopes and uses canonical current workflow data instead of legacy status-field inconsistencies.
20	- **Users and permissions:** Every application user can generate and download project exports. *(This is directly contradicted by the API's own project/export-authorization requirement — see Gaps.)*
21	- **UI behavior:**
22	  - Within Reporting > Exports, display one card for each export: Papers CSV (all active project Papers; includes Paper key, title, DOI/URL, preview, abstract, and year); Screening phase exclusions CSV (Papers finally excluded during Screening; includes Paper metadata, excluding actor, exclusion criterion, and note when available); Classification exclusions CSV (Papers excluded during Classification/Data Extraction; includes Paper metadata, excluding actor, criterion, and note when available); Classification/Data Extraction results CSV (Papers with a saved active Classification/Data Extraction record; includes Paper metadata and saved extraction values); All Papers BibTeX (all active Papers with stored BibTeX content); Included Papers BibTeX (Papers with a current final Included outcome); Excluded Papers BibTeX (Papers with a current final Excluded outcome).
23	  - Each card displays a short description of its scope, the current number of matching Papers, and a "Generate and download" action. On selection: show a blocking generation state; download the file when generation succeeds; display a safe error message when generation fails.
24	- **API behavior:**
25	  - Enforce current project context and export permission. Provide one operation to generate and stream each allowed CSV or BibTeX export.
26	  - For every export: resolve the export scope server-side; query only the current Project DB; use the fixed fields defined for that export type; generate UTF-8 CSV with correct escaping for separators, quotes, and line breaks; return the generated file directly to the browser; never accept a filesystem path or filename from the client; do not persist the generated file, its content, or a download URL; write an audit event containing export type, actor, timestamp, and exported Paper count.
27	- **Data model:** No generated-file, export-job, worker-job, retention, or artifact tables are required. Reuse existing Project DB records for: Papers; Screening outcomes and exclusion data; Classification/Data Extraction records and exclusions; stored BibTeX content. Store a lightweight export audit event only.
28	- **Acceptance criteria:**
29	  - [ ] Authorised users can directly download each supported CSV and BibTeX export.
30	  - [ ] Papers CSV contains all active project Papers.
31	  - [ ] Classification/Data Extraction CSV contains only Papers with saved active extraction data.
32	  - [ ] Included and Excluded BibTeX exports use the current final Paper outcome.
33	  - [ ] Exclusion CSV exports include available exclusion details.
34	  - [ ] Every export is isolated to the current project.
35	  - [ ] Generated files are downloaded immediately and are not retained on the server.
36	  - [ ] No worker, export history, retry, expiry, revoke, or path-based download flow is implemented.
37	- **Assigned to:** Empty
38	- **Severity:** Empty
39	- **Blocked by:** Empty
40	- **Jobs behavior:** Empty
41	- **Audit:** Empty
42	
43	## Objective and summarized requirements
44	
45	Generate and stream CSV/BibTeX directly without storing exported files.
46	
47	## Proposed prerequisites
48	
49	- [24 — Implement Project Paper List](24-paper-list.md)
50	- [30 — Implement Screening Assignment and Reviewer Decision Flow](30-screening.md)
51	- [35 — Implement Classification Assignment and Classification Workspace](35-classification.md)
52	
53	The dependencies above are implementation inferences. The original Notion relation is preserved separately; any cycles have not been removed.
54	
55	## Step-by-step instructions for the LLM
56	
57	1. Define operations by export type, authorized within the current project; reject client-supplied paths or filenames.
58	2. Create cards for Papers CSV; Screening exclusions CSV; Classification exclusions CSV; Classification/Data Extraction results CSV; and All/Included/Excluded BibTeX.
59	3. Resolve scope on the server: active Papers; final Screening exclusions; Classification exclusions; active saved classifications; stored BibTeX and current outcomes.
60	4. CSV includes the specified fixed fields: key/title/DOI/URL/preview/abstract/year and, depending on the export, exclusion actor/criterion/note or extracted values.
61	5. Generate UTF-8 with separator/quote/newline escaping; stream directly and display generation status/safe errors on the client.
62	6. Audit type, actor, timestamp, and count; create no job, artifact history, expiry/revoke flow, or persisted URL.
63	
64	## Definition of Done — completion checklist
65	
66	Notion's Acceptance criteria (reproduced above) is the primary source; the items below restate it as concrete, testable points and add detail grounded in the API behavior/UI behavior fields — note the Users-and-permissions contradiction flagged in Gaps.
67	
68	- [ ] Every export endpoint enforces current project context and an actual export permission check server-side — "every application user" from Users and permissions is not implemented literally; only authorised (project-scoped) users can trigger a generation (see Gaps for how this was resolved).
69	- [ ] Each of the seven export cards (Papers CSV; Screening exclusions CSV; Classification exclusions CSV; Classification/Data Extraction results CSV; All/Included/Excluded BibTeX) resolves its scope entirely server-side from the current Project DB — the client supplies no filter, path, or filename.
70	- [ ] Papers CSV contains exactly all active project Papers with key, title, DOI/URL, preview, abstract, and year.
71	- [ ] Screening/Classification exclusion CSVs contain only Papers finally excluded by that respective workflow, including the excluding actor, criterion, and note when available.
72	- [ ] Classification/Data Extraction results CSV contains only Papers with a saved **active** extraction/classification record, including the saved extraction values.
73	- [ ] Included/Excluded BibTeX exports use the Paper's **current final** outcome (not a stale/cached one) — a Paper whose outcome has since changed reflects the new outcome on the next export.
74	- [ ] Generated CSV is valid UTF-8 with correct escaping for the configured separator, quotes, and embedded line breaks (verify with a fixture containing a comma/quote/newline inside a field).
75	- [ ] The file streams directly to the browser as the HTTP response — it is never written to disk, object storage, or any persisted location, and no download URL is ever generated or returned.
76	- [ ] Every generation writes a lightweight audit event with export type, actor, timestamp, and exported Paper count — nothing more (no job record, no retry/expiry/revoke state).
77	- [ ] The UI shows a blocking generation state during the request and a safe, non-technical error message on failure (never a raw stack trace or DB error).
78	- [ ] Automated tests cover: each of the seven scopes returning the exact expected Paper set against a seeded fixture; CSV escaping correctness; and a rejected generation attempt for an unauthorised caller.
79	- [ ] Report which commands were run and their actual results, and explicitly record the authorization policy actually implemented for "every application user" per the decision in Gaps.
80	
81	## Gaps and pending decisions
82	
83	Users and permissions says every application user can generate exports, but the API behavior requires project/export authorization — a direct contradiction on this card. Define whether this covers all project members, Guests, or an authorized public audience (e.g., for a Published project) before implementing, per [pending decisions](PENDING-DECISIONS.md) item 14. This task's "no job/no persistence" contract also conflicts with the generic jobs/storage platform's expectation of persisted exports ([06](06-job-platform.md)/[07](07-storage.md)) — follow this ticket's specific direct-streaming contract, not the generic one, once the decision above is recorded.
84

## Full Notion card content (fetched 2026-09-28)

- **Status:** Backlog
- **Description:** Provide direct project-scoped CSV and BibTeX exports from the Reporting area. The new relis keeps the export scopes provided by legacy ReLiS, but generates the requested file from the current Project DB and downloads it immediately. Generated files are not stored, reused, or made available through predictable server paths.
- **Functional Domain:** Reporting & Export
- **Behavior:** Legacy ReLiS provides: a CSV export of all active Papers; a CSV export of Papers excluded during Screening; a CSV export of Papers excluded during Classification/Data Extraction; a CSV export of completed Classification/Data Extraction results; BibTeX exports for all, included, and excluded Papers. The new relis keeps these export scopes and uses canonical current workflow data instead of legacy status-field inconsistencies.
- **Users and permissions:** Every application user can generate and download project exports. *(This is directly contradicted by the API's own project/export-authorization requirement — see Gaps.)*
- **UI behavior:**
  - Within Reporting > Exports, display one card for each export: Papers CSV (all active project Papers; includes Paper key, title, DOI/URL, preview, abstract, and year); Screening phase exclusions CSV (Papers finally excluded during Screening; includes Paper metadata, excluding actor, exclusion criterion, and note when available); Classification exclusions CSV (Papers excluded during Classification/Data Extraction; includes Paper metadata, excluding actor, criterion, and note when available); Classification/Data Extraction results CSV (Papers with a saved active Classification/Data Extraction record; includes Paper metadata and saved extraction values); All Papers BibTeX (all active Papers with stored BibTeX content); Included Papers BibTeX (Papers with a current final Included outcome); Excluded Papers BibTeX (Papers with a current final Excluded outcome).
  - Each card displays a short description of its scope, the current number of matching Papers, and a "Generate and download" action. On selection: show a blocking generation state; download the file when generation succeeds; display a safe error message when generation fails.
- **API behavior:**
  - Enforce current project context and export permission. Provide one operation to generate and stream each allowed CSV or BibTeX export.
  - For every export: resolve the export scope server-side; query only the current Project DB; use the fixed fields defined for that export type; generate UTF-8 CSV with correct escaping for separators, quotes, and line breaks; return the generated file directly to the browser; never accept a filesystem path or filename from the client; do not persist the generated file, its content, or a download URL; write an audit event containing export type, actor, timestamp, and exported Paper count.
- **Data model:** No generated-file, export-job, worker-job, retention, or artifact tables are required. Reuse existing Project DB records for: Papers; Screening outcomes and exclusion data; Classification/Data Extraction records and exclusions; stored BibTeX content. Store a lightweight export audit event only.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - [ ] Authorised users can directly download each supported CSV and BibTeX export.
  - [ ] Papers CSV contains all active project Papers.
  - [ ] Classification/Data Extraction CSV contains only Papers with saved active extraction data.
  - [ ] Included and Excluded BibTeX exports use the current final Paper outcome.
  - [ ] Exclusion CSV exports include available exclusion details.
  - [ ] Every export is isolated to the current project.
  - [ ] Generated files are downloaded immediately and are not retained on the server.
  - [ ] No worker, export history, retry, expiry, revoke, or path-based download flow is implemented.
- **Assigned to:** Empty
- **Severity:** Empty
- **Blocked by:** Empty
- **Jobs behavior:** Empty
- **Audit:** Empty

## Objective and summarized requirements

Generate and stream CSV/BibTeX directly without storing exported files.

## Proposed prerequisites

- [24 — Implement Project Paper List](24-paper-list.md)
- [30 — Implement Screening Assignment and Reviewer Decision Flow](30-screening.md)
- [35 — Implement Classification Assignment and Classification Workspace](35-classification.md)

The dependencies above are implementation inferences. The original Notion relation is preserved separately; any cycles have not been removed.

## Step-by-step instructions for the LLM

1. Define operations by export type, authorized within the current project; reject client-supplied paths or filenames.
2. Create cards for Papers CSV; Screening exclusions CSV; Classification exclusions CSV; Classification/Data Extraction results CSV; and All/Included/Excluded BibTeX.
3. Resolve scope on the server: active Papers; final Screening exclusions; Classification exclusions; active saved classifications; stored BibTeX and current outcomes.
4. CSV includes the specified fixed fields: key/title/DOI/URL/preview/abstract/year and, depending on the export, exclusion actor/criterion/note or extracted values.
5. Generate UTF-8 with separator/quote/newline escaping; stream directly and display generation status/safe errors on the client.
6. Audit type, actor, timestamp, and count; create no job, artifact history, expiry/revoke flow, or persisted URL.

## Definition of Done — completion checklist

Notion's Acceptance criteria (reproduced above) is the primary source; the items below restate it as concrete, testable points and add detail grounded in the API behavior/UI behavior fields — note the Users-and-permissions contradiction flagged in Gaps.

- [ ] Every export endpoint enforces current project context and an actual export permission check server-side — "every application user" from Users and permissions is not implemented literally; only authorised (project-scoped) users can trigger a generation (see Gaps for how this was resolved).
- [ ] Each of the seven export cards (Papers CSV; Screening exclusions CSV; Classification exclusions CSV; Classification/Data Extraction results CSV; All/Included/Excluded BibTeX) resolves its scope entirely server-side from the current Project DB — the client supplies no filter, path, or filename.
- [ ] Papers CSV contains exactly all active project Papers with key, title, DOI/URL, preview, abstract, and year.
- [ ] Screening/Classification exclusion CSVs contain only Papers finally excluded by that respective workflow, including the excluding actor, criterion, and note when available.
- [ ] Classification/Data Extraction results CSV contains only Papers with a saved **active** extraction/classification record, including the saved extraction values.
- [ ] Included/Excluded BibTeX exports use the Paper's **current final** outcome (not a stale/cached one) — a Paper whose outcome has since changed reflects the new outcome on the next export.
- [ ] Generated CSV is valid UTF-8 with correct escaping for the configured separator, quotes, and embedded line breaks (verify with a fixture containing a comma/quote/newline inside a field).
- [ ] The file streams directly to the browser as the HTTP response — it is never written to disk, object storage, or any persisted location, and no download URL is ever generated or returned.
- [ ] Every generation writes a lightweight audit event with export type, actor, timestamp, and exported Paper count — nothing more (no job record, no retry/expiry/revoke state).
- [ ] The UI shows a blocking generation state during the request and a safe, non-technical error message on failure (never a raw stack trace or DB error).
- [ ] Automated tests cover: each of the seven scopes returning the exact expected Paper set against a seeded fixture; CSV escaping correctness; and a rejected generation attempt for an unauthorised caller.
- [ ] Report which commands were run and their actual results, and explicitly record the authorization policy actually implemented for "every application user" per the decision in Gaps.

## Gaps and pending decisions

Users and permissions says every application user can generate exports, but the API behavior requires project/export authorization — a direct contradiction on this card. Define whether this covers all project members, Guests, or an authorized public audience (e.g., for a Published project) before implementing, per [pending decisions](PENDING-DECISIONS.md) item 14. This task's "no job/no persistence" contract also conflicts with the generic jobs/storage platform's expectation of persisted exports ([06](06-job-platform.md)/[07](07-storage.md)) — follow this ticket's specific direct-streaming contract, not the generic one, once the decision above is recorded.

227	| Identity | Core user, credentials, tokens, external identity | None — explicit negative (13) | Profile image bytes; JWT signing keys (secret config) | Account-status enum representation (§3.1) |
228	| Session | Session/revocation record | None | JWT signing keys (secret config) | Revoke-all mechanism (§3.2) |
229	| Project | Registry, metadata, lifecycle, provisioning state | None until ready; then project-runtime data only (19 — Data model) | Cover image bytes (inferred) | Project↔Project-DB connection mapping (§3.3, gap) |
230	| Membership | All of it | **Explicit none** (15 — Data model) | — | Role enum (`PROJECT_OWNER` vs. `PROJECT_ADMIN`), §5.1 |
231	| Invitation | All of it | None | Email delivery via job platform | Expiry period value + storage location (§5.3, §3.5) |
232	| Draft | All of it (JSONB) | None — explicit negative (18) | — | Post-conversion disposition (§3.6, gap) |
233	| Job | Application metadata | None mentioned | pg-boss's own tables (co-located, not modeled here); result artifacts via storage (07) | Queue engine itself remains undecided (PENDING-DECISIONS item 1) — not resolved here |
234	| Audit | Control-plane `AuditEvent` + cross-project correlation | Project-resource `AuditEvent` + `OperationBatch`/`CompensatingAction` | — | Cross-project correlation mechanism (§5.9, gap) |
235	
236	This table is a summary index only — §3's per-field rows are authoritative;
237	consult them before treating any cell here as a finalized decision.
238	
239	## 5. Contradictions, missing information, and decision gates
240	
241	Each item lists the conflicting sources, every affected consumer, the
242	precise question a decision must answer, and exactly what downstream schema
243	work it blocks. None of these is resolved by this document; recording them
244	does not authorize picking a side.
245	
246	**5.1 — `PROJECT_OWNER` vs. `PROJECT_ADMIN` (role model).** Conflicting
247	sources: [15 — Data model/Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/15-membership.md)
248	(five-value role enum headed by `PROJECT_ADMIN`, membership statuses
249	`ACTIVE`/`REMOVED` only) vs. [18 — Users and permissions/API behavior](../../../context/notion-tasks/18-protocol-wizard.md)
250	(a protected `PROJECT_OWNER`, a `PENDING_PROVISIONING` status, and a
251	backend-enforced correspondence to `Project.createdByUserId`); also named in
252	[21 — Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/21-project-settings.md)
253	(`PROJECT_OWNER` as the only General-settings-authorized role) and
254	[PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
255	Affected consumers: 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 22 (audit role-mapping), 23.
256	Precise question: is `PROJECT_OWNER` (a) an alias asserted over the existing
257	`PROJECT_ADMIN` value, (b) a distinct, protected sixth role sitting above
258	`PROJECT_ADMIN`, or (c) the sole protected creator role with `PROJECT_ADMIN`
259	demoted to an ordinary assignable role? Blocks: the `Membership.role` enum,
260	the membership-status enum (two vs. more values), and every "last protected
261	member" guard — all of 03.04's schema work on this table. **Deferred
262	entirely to [03.03](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md)**, per
263	this sub-issue's explicit instruction not to finalize role enums here.
264	
265	**5.2 — Last Project Manager vs. last Project Admin guard.** Conflicting
266	sources: both **within guide 15 itself** — Acceptance criteria ("Removing
267	the last Project Admin is rejected") vs. API behavior ("does not violate the
268	last-Project-Manager guard"); also [PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
269	Affected consumers: 15 only (but the guard logic is foundational to
270	membership removal/role-change validation). Precise question: which
271	role(s) — Manager, Admin, Owner, or more than one independently — trigger a
272	"cannot remove the last one" rejection? Blocks: membership removal/role-change
273	validation logic in 03.04; overlaps with 5.1 since the answer likely depends
274	on how `PROJECT_OWNER` is finally modeled.
275	
276	**5.3 — Invitation expiry: 7 days vs. 48 hours.** Conflicting sources: 15 —
277	UI/API behavior (7-day default, admin-configurable) vs. 15 — Jobs behavior
278	(48 hours); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 3](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
279	Affected consumers: 15 (token generation, UI display, scheduled cleanup); 23
280	(if the value is meant to be admin-configurable, its storage key is also
281	undefined — see §3.5). Precise question: is the default 7 days (configurable)
282	or a fixed 48 hours, and is it configurable at all? Blocks: `Invitation`'s
283	expiry default/validation and the scheduled-cleanup job's cutoff logic.
284	
285	**5.4 — Who may create a project.** Conflicting sources: 19 — Behavior ("any
286	authenticated user can start a project-creation draft") vs. 18 — Users and
287	permissions ("users with project-creation permission can start... a draft");
288	[PENDING-DECISIONS item 6](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
289	Affected consumers: 18, 19. Precise question: is draft/project creation open
290	to every authenticated user, or gated by a permission/role that no source
291	names explicitly? Blocks: whether `Draft` creation needs an authorization
292	check against a field that does not yet exist anywhere in this inventory (a
293	"can-create-projects" flag/role has no source-named representation).
294	
295	**5.5 — Project ownership/administration access matrix.** Conflicting
296	sources: 19 — Gaps (creator-plus-Application-Administrator access alternates
297	with owner-only editing) and 21 — Gaps (Owner-only per Users/permissions vs.
298	Project-Manager-inclusive per UI behavior's "Access rules"); [PENDING-DECISIONS
299	items 6 and 11](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md). Affected
300	consumers: 19, 21. Precise question: the exact per-action/per-tab
301	authorization matrix for Owner/Manager/Admin. Blocks: mostly an
302	authorization-layer decision, not a schema field — but it determines whether
303	any "settings access grant" needs its own schema representation at all
304	(current reading: no — authorization is role-derived, not a separate grant
305	table — but this is itself only an inference pending the decision).
306	
307	**5.6 — Direct settings vs. a protocol-revision/activation job (guide 21's
308	own self-contradiction).** Conflicting sources, all within 21: Description/
309	most of UI behavior/API behavior/Acceptance-criteria-prose (no
310	revision/version-comparison/activation/rollback UI) vs. 21 — Jobs behavior
311	(describes an "idempotent revision job," "persist validation, impact,
312	progress, and failure reports for the revision," and "duplicate protocol
313	versions"); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 11](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
314	Affected consumers: 21, 23 (which explicitly warns its own labels/settings
315	revision model "must not reintroduce protocol revisions prohibited in
316	[21]"). Precise question: does Project Settings ever need any
317	version/revision/activation data model, or is it strictly direct-editing
318	with only `createdBy`/`createdAt`/`modifiedBy` columns and no history beyond
319	that? Blocks: whether any Project DB protocol table needs version/revision
320	columns at all — directly relevant to this sub-issue's instruction not to
321	introduce drafts/revisions where a consuming task prohibits them, since 21
322	prohibits them in its majority text while its own Jobs behavior field
323	contradicts that.
324	
325	**5.7 — Project DB connection-mapping storage (missing information, not a
326	conflict).** No source states this. [17 — Data model](../../../context/notion-tasks/17-project-resolver.md)
327	is entirely empty ("Data model: Empty"); [16 — Data model](../../../context/notion-tasks/16-project-template.md)
328	lists provisioning metadata but no explicit "physical database
329	identifier/connection reference" field, even though 16 — API behavior is
330	explicit that this value must never be exposed to a client. Affected
331	consumers: 16, 17. Precise question: where and in what form is the mapping
332	from `projectId` to its physical, ready Project DB persisted? Blocks: the
333	resolver's schema cannot be designed in 03.04 without this; recommend
334	obtaining a decision (or an explicit "to be designed in 03.04 without a
335	source answer, flagged as an engineering decision") before finalizing the
336	Control DB project-registry table.
337	
338	**5.8 — Invitation-validity-period storage location (missing information).**
339	15 — UI behavior names an Application-Administrator-configured value; 23 —
340	Data model only describes a generic, keyless "typed global settings"
341	registry. Affected consumers: 15, 23. Precise question: is this a
342	`SystemSetting` row (keyed how?), a dedicated Control DB column on some
343	other table, or a literal constant? Blocks: `Invitation.expirationTime`'s
344	computation — low severity, since a literal default can stand in once 5.3 is
345	resolved, but the configurability requirement itself remains unimplemented
346	until this is answered.
347	
348	**5.9 — Cross-project audit correlation mechanism (missing information).**
349	22 — Data model names "cross-project operation correlation metadata" in the
350	Control DB without defining its shape, while the actual `OperationBatch`/
351	`CompensatingAction` records live per-project. Affected consumers: 22.
352	Precise question: what exact Control DB record lets an Application
353	Administrator search/filter operation history across every Project DB
354	without fanning out to each one at query time? Blocks: the `AuditEvent`/
355	correlation schema design in 03.04 — this is a real architectural question,
356	not merely a field-naming one.
357	
358	**5.10 — Draft-to-Project conversion disposition (missing information).** No
359	source (18's Data model/API behavior, or 19) states what happens to a
360	`Draft` row after its wizard confirmation successfully creates a `Project`.
361	Affected consumers: 18, 19 (which shows *unfinished* drafts in "My projects"
362	but never addresses finished ones). Precise question: is the Draft row
363	deleted, archived, or retained and linked to the resulting Project for
364	history? Blocks: `Draft` entity lifecycle/retention design in 03.04.
365	
366	Documenting these ten items does not block the rest of this inventory —
367	every other field in §3 that is not cited above is unaffected and can
368	proceed to 03.04 design once 03.03's role decision lands.
369	
370	## 6. Planned verification scenarios (NOT executed — proposals for 03.04/03.05)
371	
372	These are derived directly from the constraints recorded in §3 and are
373	explicitly **not** automated tests, not run, and not evidence of any
374	behavior today — they are a forward-looking checklist for whoever implements
375	and tests the eventual schema/repositories.
376	
377	- **Identity:** duplicate normalized username/email rejected at the data
378	  layer; archiving the last active Application Administrator rejected;
379	  archived user cannot authenticate; email-verification token is single-use
380	  and a second request invalidates the first; password-reset token same;
381	  Google `ExternalIdentity` lookup by `(provider, sub)` never matches by
382	  email alone.
383	- **Session:** a revoked session is rejected even with a non-expired,
384	  signature-valid token; a password change/reset invalidates every other
385	  active session for that account, not only the current one.
386	- **Project:** project short-name uniqueness enforced at the data layer
387	  (not only client-side); repeating the same provisioning idempotency key
388	  does not create a second project/database/membership; a non-owner cannot
389	  mutate project metadata; an archived project rejects writes at the API
390	  layer.
391	- **Membership:** at most one active membership per `(projectId, userId)`
392	  enforced at the data layer; removing the last protected member (per
393	  whichever role 03.03 settles on) is rejected; a Project Manager cannot
394	  remove a Project Admin/Owner; removing a membership never deletes the
395	  underlying User row.
396	- **Invitation:** at most one active invitation per `(projectId,
397	  normalizedEmail)` enforced at the data layer; resending invalidates the
398	  prior token; an expired invitation cannot be accepted; accepting requires
399	  verified ownership of the invited email and never silently changes the
400	  stored role.
401	- **Draft:** a draft is resumable only by its creator or an audited
402	  Application Administrator; a draft alone never creates a Project DB
403	  connection or row; final confirmation with a repeated idempotency key
404	  returns the existing result rather than duplicating anything.
405	- **Job:** enqueuing the same idempotency key twice does not create a
406	  second job; `listJobs` never leaks another project's jobs to a Project
407	  Admin; a job payload never contains a credential-shaped value.
408	- **Audit:** no code path updates or hard-deletes an `AuditEvent`; a
409	  control-plane event and a project-resource event for the same logical
410	  action are both recorded (not merged into one row); a `CompensatingAction`
411	  preview that said "safe" is re-validated (and can still be rejected) at
412	  execution time if state changed in between.
413	
414	## 7. Handoff checklist for 03.03, 03.04, and 03.05
415	
416	- [ ] **03.03** must resolve §5.1 (`PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN`) and, as
417	      part of the same decision, should address §5.2 (which role(s) the
418	      "last protected member" guard protects) since both hinge on the same
419	      role model. Do not finalize the `Membership.role` or
420	      `Membership.status` enum before this lands.
421	- [ ] **03.04** (schema/migrations/client) should treat §3's **explicit**
422	      rows as the primary input, **inference** rows as needing an explicit
423	      note in the schema/PR description (not silent adoption), and must
424	      obtain a decision — or record an explicit, reported engineering
425	      choice — for every **unspecified**/gap item in §5 before encoding it,
426	      per this task's "do not silently treat an unresolved requirement as
427	      settled" instruction. §5.7 (Project DB connection mapping) and §5.9
428	      (cross-project audit correlation) are the two gaps most likely to
429	      require real architectural design work, not just a field name.
430	- [ ] **03.04** must keep the Control DB / Project DB / External boundaries
431	      in §4 intact: no membership/identity/session data in any Project DB
432	      (15's explicit negative); no protocol/settings data duplicated into
433	      the Control DB beyond the specific fields §3.3/§3.6 name (project
434	      metadata + research-question order only); `AuditEvent` modeled
435	      separately per database, never as one shared table; pg-boss's own
436	      tables left alone — only the companion job-metadata model from §3.7
437	      is this inventory's concern.
438	- [ ] **03.05** (typed repositories) should expose repository boundaries
439	      aligned to §3's eight domains rather than one generic data-access
440	      surface — e.g. a membership repository must not also expose raw
441	      invitation-token or credential operations, consistent with the parent
442	      card's "do not expose generic CRUD" requirement.
443	- [ ] Any schema element introduced in 03.04 that cannot be traced to a row
444	      in §3, or to a decision recorded in §5, should be treated as scope
445	      expansion requiring its own justification — this inventory is meant to
446	      make that check straightforward.
447	
448	## Acceptance-criteria evidence (for this sub-issue, 03.02)
449	
450	- **Every listed field/relation has a source or an explicit inference/decision
451	  label:** every row in §3's eight tables carries a Status column value
452	  (explicit / inference / conflicting / unspecified) and a Source column
453	  citing the exact guide and section it was reproduced from.
454	- **All eight requested domains are accounted for, including explicit
455	  "unspecified" findings:** §3.1–§3.8 cover identity, session, project,
456	  membership, invitation, draft, job, and audit in order; each contains at
457	  least one row explicitly labeled "unspecified" or flagged as a gap where
458	  the sources leave a representation undefined (e.g. §3.1's account-status
459	  enum, §3.3's connection-mapping gap, §3.6's draft-disposition gap, §3.8's
460	  correlation-mechanism gap).
461	- **Undefined role and ownership semantics are flagged before constraints
462	  are proposed:** §5.1/§5.2 record the `PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN` and
463	  last-protected-member conflicts without proposing a resolution, and §3.4's
464	  role-enum row is explicitly marked "conflicting" rather than defaulting to
465	  either source's version.
466	- **No business schema or repository implementation is introduced:** this
467	  document contains no Prisma syntax, no TypeScript interface, and no code
468	  change; §2 confirms `@relis/contracts` and `@relis/database` are unchanged
469	  from the 03.01 baseline.
470	- **No unresolved requirement is silently treated as settled:** §5's ten
471	  items are each phrased as an open question with affected consumers and
472	  blocked downstream work, not as a chosen interpretation; §6's scenarios
473	  are explicitly labeled "NOT executed."

# Control DB contracts — consolidated requirements inventory

Local sub-issue: [03.02 — Consolidate the Control DB contracts required by
consuming tasks](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-02.md), under
parent [03 — Create control Prisma schema](../../../context/notion-tasks/03-control-prisma.md).

## 0. Purpose and boundaries

This document consolidates, with full traceability, every field, relation,
lifecycle state, and constraint that a local consuming-task guide explicitly
requires for the eight areas this sub-issue covers: **identity, session,
project, membership, invitation, draft, job, audit**. It is an **inspection
and documentation deliverable only**:

- It does **not** define, approve, or implement a Prisma schema. No model,
  field name, or type below is a finalized schema element — each is labeled
  by its evidentiary status (explicit / engineering inference / conflicting
  / unspecified) and traced to the exact guide and field it comes from.
- It does **not** resolve the `PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN` conflict or any
  other contradiction found below — those are recorded as decision gates for
  [03.03](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md) (role/ownership)
  and, where schema-relevant but not role-related, flagged for 03.04 to
  resolve with the user before implementation.
- No implementation code, Prisma schema, migration, generated client, or
  package export was changed to produce this document.

It builds on, and does not duplicate, [`control-database-inventory.md`](control-database-inventory.md)
(sub-issue 03.01's verified baseline: `@relis/database`'s current empty
state, the migration entry point, and existing test coverage) — consult that
document for the current-state package/Prisma/test inventory.

## 1. Scope and source inventory

**Sources read in full for this document** (all local; no Notion, GitHub, or
other external browsing was performed, per this task's instructions):

- [`control-database-inventory.md`](control-database-inventory.md) (03.01 baseline).
- [`packages/contracts/package.json`](../../packages/contracts/package.json) and
  [`packages/contracts/src/index.ts`](../../packages/contracts/src/index.ts) (code-inspected).
- [`context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md`](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md) (items 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 11, 19 are directly relevant here and are cited by number throughout).
- Consuming-task guides, read in full:
  [06 — job platform](../../../context/notion-tasks/06-job-platform.md),
  [07 — storage](../../../context/notion-tasks/07-storage.md),
  [08 — installation/demo](../../../context/notion-tasks/08-installation-demo.md),
  [09 — login/sessions](../../../context/notion-tasks/09-login-sessions.md),
  [10 — registration](../../../context/notion-tasks/10-registration.md),
  [11 — password reset](../../../context/notion-tasks/11-password-reset.md),
  [12 — profile](../../../context/notion-tasks/12-profile.md),
  [13 — admin users](../../../context/notion-tasks/13-admin-users.md),
  [14 — Google OIDC](../../../context/notion-tasks/14-google-oidc.md),
  [15 — membership](../../../context/notion-tasks/15-membership.md),
  [16 — project template/provisioning](../../../context/notion-tasks/16-project-template.md),
  [17 — project DB resolver](../../../context/notion-tasks/17-project-resolver.md),
  [18 — protocol wizard](../../../context/notion-tasks/18-protocol-wizard.md),
  [19 — project lifecycle](../../../context/notion-tasks/19-project-lifecycle.md),
  [20 — project workspace](../../../context/notion-tasks/20-project-workspace.md) (Data model section only, for its one Control DB addition),
  [21 — project settings](../../../context/notion-tasks/21-project-settings.md),
  [22 — audit/undo](../../../context/notion-tasks/22-audit-undo.md),
  [23 — system settings](../../../context/notion-tasks/23-system-settings.md) (read as a cross-reference for where configuration values named by other guides — e.g. invitation validity, registration mode, Google OIDC enablement — are likely owned; **not** one of this sub-issue's eight domains).

**Citation convention:** every row below cites a guide file and the exact
Notion-card field it was reproduced under (e.g. "15 — Data model", "18 — API
behavior"). These are the guides' own reproduced section names, not new
numbering invented here.

**Status labels used throughout** (per this sub-issue's AC requirement that
every field carry one):

- **explicit** — stated directly in a source field.
- **inference** — a reasonable engineering consequence of an explicit
  requirement, not itself stated (e.g., a field needed to implement a stated
  behavior, but whose name/shape the source never gives).
- **conflicting** — two or more sources disagree; see §5 for the decision
  gate.
- **unspecified** — a behavior is explicitly required but its data
  representation is not given anywhere in the read sources; recorded as a
  gap, not invented.

## 2. Implemented contracts vs. future requirements

- **`@relis/contracts`** ([`package.json`](../../packages/contracts/package.json),
  [`src/index.ts`](../../packages/contracts/src/index.ts)) exists and is
  workspace-registered, but its entire source is `export { z } from "zod";`
  — it re-exports the Zod library itself and defines **zero** domain
  schemas. A repository-wide search for `@relis/contracts` as an imported
  specifier found no consumers anywhere in `apps/*` or `packages/*` — nothing
  currently imports it.
- **`@relis/database`**: per the 03.01 baseline, `index.ts` is `export {};`
  and both Prisma schemas are model-free (see that document's §2–§3 for full
  detail; not repeated here).
- **Conclusion: every field, contract, and relation in §3 below is a future
  requirement.** Nothing in this inventory has an implemented counterpart in
  this checkout today. This document does not change that — it is the input
  03.04/03.05 will design against.

## 3. Field-and-relation traceability matrices

Each table's **Ownership** column uses: **Control DB**, **Project DB**,
**External** (object storage, the job queue's own internal tables, or
managed secret/key configuration — never a Prisma model in either database),
or **Unresolved**.

### 3.1 Identity (User, Credential, ExternalIdentity)

| Field / relation | Source (file — section) | Behavior requiring persistence | Ownership | Constraints | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| User: immutable ID | 15 — Data model | Every reference from membership, invitation, session, audit | Control DB | Immutable | explicit |
| User: unique normalized username | 15 — Data model | Exact-match lookup for adding/inviting members (15 — API behavior); admin directory search (13 — UI behavior) | Control DB | Unique, normalized | explicit |
| User: unique normalized email | 15 — Data model | Login (09), registration (10), reset (11), profile email change (12), Google-identity email check (14) | Control DB | Unique, normalized | explicit |
| User: email-verification state | 15 — Data model; 10 — Behavior; 14 — API behavior ("require the email to be provider-verified") | Gates protected-feature access until verified (10 — Users/permissions) | Control DB | — | explicit (exact enum values not given) |
| User: account status (active / archived / disabled / unverified) | 15 — Data model ("account status"); 09 — Users/permissions (rejects archived/disabled/unverified); 13 — Data model ("active/archive state") | Login eligibility gate (09); admin archive/restore (13) | Control DB | Archived users cannot log in or receive new assignments but keep historical attribution (13) | explicit behavior, **unspecified** representation — sources name at least 3 overlapping states (archived/disabled/unverified) without stating whether they are one enum or independent flags |
| User: Application-Administrator authority (global role) | 13 — Data model ("global roles") | Gates system-wide user directory and settings access (13, 23) | Control DB | The final active Application Administrator cannot be archived or demoted (13 — Acceptance criteria) | explicit — distinct from the project-scoped role in §3.3, not the same enum |
| User: timestamps | 15 — Data model | Audit, directory sorting | Control DB | — | explicit (generic, no field names given) |
| Credential: password hash | 09 — Data model | Login verification | Control DB | `crypto.scrypt`, constant-time compare | explicit |
| Credential: scrypt parameter version | 09 — Data model | Triggers rehash after login when parameters are upgraded | Control DB | Versioned | explicit |
| Credential: per-credential random salt | 09 — Data model | Password hashing | Control DB | ≥16 bytes, cryptographically random | explicit |
| Credential: last-login audit data | 09 — Data model | — | Control DB | — | explicit, unspecified exact shape |
| (JWT signing keys) | 09 — Data model | Session issuance/validation | **External** (managed secret/key config) | Must include a `kid`; explicitly **not** a database field | explicit |
| Email-verification token: digest, expiry, consumed timestamp, retry metadata | 10 — Data model | `register`/`verify-email`/`resend-verification` | Control DB | Single-use, expiring, digest only (never plaintext); new token invalidates the previous one | explicit |
| Registration audit data | 10 — Data model | — | Control DB | — | explicit, but possibly redundant with the general `AuditEvent` model in §3.8 — unclear whether this is a distinct field set or just means "an `AuditEvent` is written"; **unspecified** |
| Registration mode (public / disabled / admin-managed) | 10 — Behavior/API behavior | Gates which registration path is active | **Unresolved** | — | explicit requirement, but likely owned by the system-settings registry (23 — Data model: "typed global settings"), not a User/identity field — out of this sub-issue's 8 domains; flagged, not assigned |
| Password-reset token: digest, expiry, consumption metadata | 11 — Data model | `request-password-reset`/`validate-reset-token`/`complete-reset` | Control DB | Single-use, digest only, same pattern as §10's token | explicit |
| Force-reset flag "where needed" | 11 — Data model | `administrator-force-reset` | Control DB | Administrator never sees/sets the password or token | explicit requirement, **inference** on representation — the source's own hedge ("where needed") leaves open whether this is a persisted flag or purely a code path |
| Profile: display/profile fields | 12 — Data model | `get-my-profile`/`update-my-profile` | Control DB | Editable-field allowlist excludes authority/role/status/verification (12 — Users/permissions) | explicit requirement, **unspecified** which exact fields ("profile fields" is generic; 12's own Acceptance criteria are empty) |
