## 5. Contradictions, missing information, and decision gates

Each item lists the conflicting sources, every affected consumer, the
precise question a decision must answer, and exactly what downstream schema
work it blocks. None of these is resolved by this document; recording them
does not authorize picking a side.

**5.1 — `PROJECT_OWNER` vs. `PROJECT_ADMIN` (role model).** Conflicting
sources: [15 — Data model/Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/15-membership.md)
(five-value role enum headed by `PROJECT_ADMIN`, membership statuses
`ACTIVE`/`REMOVED` only) vs. [18 — Users and permissions/API behavior](../../../context/notion-tasks/18-protocol-wizard.md)
(a protected `PROJECT_OWNER`, a `PENDING_PROVISIONING` status, and a
backend-enforced correspondence to `Project.createdByUserId`); also named in
[21 — Users and permissions](../../../context/notion-tasks/21-project-settings.md)
(`PROJECT_OWNER` as the only General-settings-authorized role) and
[PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 22 (audit role-mapping), 23.
Precise question: is `PROJECT_OWNER` (a) an alias asserted over the existing
`PROJECT_ADMIN` value, (b) a distinct, protected sixth role sitting above
`PROJECT_ADMIN`, or (c) the sole protected creator role with `PROJECT_ADMIN`
demoted to an ordinary assignable role? Blocks: the `Membership.role` enum,
the membership-status enum (two vs. more values), and every "last protected
member" guard — all of 03.04's schema work on this table. **Deferred
entirely to [03.03](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md)**, per
this sub-issue's explicit instruction not to finalize role enums here.

**5.2 — Last Project Manager vs. last Project Admin guard.** Conflicting
sources: both **within guide 15 itself** — Acceptance criteria ("Removing
the last Project Admin is rejected") vs. API behavior ("does not violate the
last-Project-Manager guard"); also [PENDING-DECISIONS item 2](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15 only (but the guard logic is foundational to
membership removal/role-change validation). Precise question: which
role(s) — Manager, Admin, Owner, or more than one independently — trigger a
"cannot remove the last one" rejection? Blocks: membership removal/role-change
validation logic in 03.04; overlaps with 5.1 since the answer likely depends
on how `PROJECT_OWNER` is finally modeled.

**5.3 — Invitation expiry: 7 days vs. 48 hours.** Conflicting sources: 15 —
UI/API behavior (7-day default, admin-configurable) vs. 15 — Jobs behavior
(48 hours); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 3](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 15 (token generation, UI display, scheduled cleanup); 23
(if the value is meant to be admin-configurable, its storage key is also
undefined — see §3.5). Precise question: is the default 7 days (configurable)
or a fixed 48 hours, and is it configurable at all? Blocks: `Invitation`'s
expiry default/validation and the scheduled-cleanup job's cutoff logic.

**5.4 — Who may create a project.** Conflicting sources: 19 — Behavior ("any
authenticated user can start a project-creation draft") vs. 18 — Users and
permissions ("users with project-creation permission can start... a draft");
[PENDING-DECISIONS item 6](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).

to every authenticated user, or gated by a permission/role that no source

"can-create-projects" flag/role has no source-named representation).

**5.5 — Project ownership/administration access matrix.** Conflicting
sources: 19 — Gaps (creator-plus-Application-Administrator access alternates
with owner-only editing) and 21 — Gaps (Owner-only per Users/permissions vs.
Project-Manager-inclusive per UI behavior's "Access rules"); [PENDING-DECISIONS
items 6 and 11](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md). Affected
consumers: 19, 21. Precise question: the exact per-action/per-tab
authorization matrix for Owner/Manager/Admin. Blocks: mostly an
authorization-layer decision, not a schema field — but it determines whether

(current reading: no — authorization is role-derived, not a separate grant
table — but this is itself only an inference pending the decision).

**5.6 — Direct settings vs. a protocol-revision/activation job (guide 21's
own self-contradiction).** Conflicting sources, all within 21: Description/
most of UI behavior/API behavior/Acceptance-criteria-prose (no
revision/version-comparison/activation/rollback UI) vs. 21 — Jobs behavior
(describes an "idempotent revision job," "persist validation, impact,
progress, and failure reports for the revision," and "duplicate protocol
versions"); [PENDING-DECISIONS item 11](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md).
Affected consumers: 21, 23 (which explicitly warns its own labels/settings
revision model "must not reintroduce protocol revisions prohibited in
[21]"). Precise question: does Project Settings ever need any
version/revision/activation data model, or is it strictly direct-editing
with only `createdBy`/`createdAt`/`modifiedBy` columns and no history beyond
that? Blocks: whether any Project DB protocol table needs version/revision
columns at all — directly relevant to this sub-issue's instruction not to
introduce drafts/revisions where a consuming task prohibits them, since 21
prohibits them in its majority text while its own Jobs behavior field

**5.7 — Project DB connection-mapping storage (missing information, not a

**5.8 — Invitation-validity-period storage location (missing information).**
15 — UI behavior names an Application-Administrator-configured value; 23 —
Data model only describes a generic, keyless "typed global settings"

`SystemSetting` row (keyed how?), a dedicated Control DB column on some
other table, or a literal constant? Blocks: `Invitation.expirationTime`'s

**5.9 — Cross-project audit correlation mechanism (missing information).**
22 — Data model names "cross-project operation correlation metadata" in the

**5.10 — Draft-to-Project conversion disposition (missing information).** No

## 6. Planned verification scenarios (NOT executed — proposals for 03.04/03.05)

These are derived directly from the constraints recorded in §3 and are
explicitly **not** automated tests, not run, and not evidence of any
behavior today — they are a forward-looking checklist for whoever implements
and tests the eventual schema/repositories.

- **Identity:** duplicate normalized username/email rejected at the data
  layer; archiving the last active Application Administrator rejected;
  archived user cannot authenticate; email-verification token is single-use
  and a second request invalidates the first; password-reset token same;
  Google `ExternalIdentity` lookup by `(provider, sub)` never matches by
  email alone.
- **Session:** a revoked session is rejected even with a non-expired,
  signature-valid token; a password change/reset invalidates every other
  active session for that account, not only the current one.
- **Project:** project short-name uniqueness enforced at the data layer
  (not only client-side); repeating the same provisioning idempotency key
  does not create a second project/database/membership; a non-owner cannot
  mutate project metadata; an archived project rejects writes at the API
  layer.
- **Membership:** at most one active membership per `(projectId, userId)`
  enforced at the data layer; removing the last protected member (per
  whichever role 03.03 settles on) is rejected; a Project Manager cannot
  remove a Project Admin/Owner; removing a membership never deletes the
  underlying User row.
- **Invitation:** at most one active invitation per `(projectId,
  normalizedEmail)` enforced at the data layer; resending invalidates the
  prior token; an expired invitation cannot be accepted; accepting requires
  verified ownership of the invited email and never silently changes the
  stored role.
- **Draft:** a draft is resumable only by its creator or an audited
  Application Administrator; a draft alone never creates a Project DB
  connection or row; final confirmation with a repeated idempotency key
  returns the existing result rather than duplicating anything.
- **Job:** enqueuing the same idempotency key twice does not create a
  second job; `listJobs` never leaks another project's jobs to a Project
  Admin; a job payload never contains a credential-shaped value.
- **Audit:** no code path updates or hard-deletes an `AuditEvent`; a
  control-plane event and a project-resource event for the same logical
  action are both recorded (not merged into one row); a `CompensatingAction`
  preview that said "safe" is re-validated (and can still be rejected) at
  execution time if state changed in between.

- [ ] **03.03** must resolve §5.1 (`PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN`) and, as
      part of the same decision, should address §5.2 (which role(s) the
      "last protected member" guard protects) since both hinge on the same
      role model. Do not finalize the `Membership.role` or
      `Membership.status` enum before this lands.
- [ ] **03.04** (schema/migrations/client) should treat §3's **explicit**
      rows as the primary input, **inference** rows as needing an explicit
      note in the schema/PR description (not silent adoption), and must
      obtain a decision — or record an explicit, reported engineering
      choice — for every **unspecified**/gap item in §5 before encoding it,
      per this task's "do not silently treat an unresolved requirement as
      settled" instruction. §5.7 (Project DB connection mapping) and §5.9
      (cross-project audit correlation) are the two gaps most likely to
      require real architectural design work, not just a field name.
- [ ] **03.04** must keep the Control DB / Project DB / External boundaries
      in §4 intact: no membership/identity/session data in any Project DB
      (15's explicit negative); no protocol/settings data duplicated into
      the Control DB beyond the specific fields §3.3/§3.6 name (project
      metadata + research-question order only); `AuditEvent` modeled
      separately per database, never as one shared table; pg-boss's own
      tables left alone — only the companion job-metadata model from §3.7
      is this inventory's concern.
- [ ] **03.05** (typed repositories) should expose repository boundaries
      aligned to §3's eight domains rather than one generic data-access
      surface — e.g. a membership repository must not also expose raw
      invitation-token or credential operations, consistent with the parent
      card's "do not expose generic CRUD" requirement.

      in §3, or to a decision recorded in §5, should be treated as scope
      expansion requiring its own justification — this inventory is meant to
      make that check straightforward.

  label:** every row in §3's eight tables carries a Status column value
  (explicit / inference / conflicting / unspecified) and a Source column
  citing the exact guide and section it was reproduced from.

  "unspecified" findings:** §3.1–§3.8 cover identity, session, project,
  membership, invitation, draft, job, and audit in order; each contains at
  least one row explicitly labeled "unspecified" or flagged as a gap where
  the sources leave a representation undefined (e.g. §3.1's account-status
  enum, §3.3's connection-mapping gap, §3.6's draft-disposition gap, §3.8's
  correlation-mechanism gap).

Work on sub-issue 03.03: Resolve the PROJECT_OWNER/PROJECT_ADMIN discrepancy before finalizing identity and membership enums and constraints.

Parent issue: Create control Prisma schema.

Objective
Produce a user-approved role/ownership decision and permission matrix that subsequent schema and repository work can implement without guessing.

Scope
Analysis and decision documentation only. Do not implement Prisma models, enums, migrations, repositories, authorization code, or application features.

Work only inside relis/. Follow repository instructions, applicable local Claude skills, and the mandatory context/project-structure.md, context/stack.yml, and context/testing-policy.md.

Use local sources only. Do not browse external services.

Starting context
- docs/architecture/control-database-inventory.md records the existing database baseline.
- docs/architecture/control-database-contracts.md consolidates requirements and unresolved decisions.
- Guide 15 describes PROJECT_ADMIN and membership states ACTIVE/REMOVED.
- Guide 18 introduces a protected PROJECT_OWNER, correspondence with Project.createdByUserId, and PENDING_PROVISIONING membership.
- Guide 15 also conflicts internally on protecting the last Project Admin versus the last Project Manager.
- Guides 19/21 contain overlapping and conflicting project-administration permissions.
- These contradictions remain unresolved. Previous documentation is not approval of any interpretation.

Phase 1 — analyze and request a decision
1. Read the baseline, consolidated contracts, relevant local guides (especially 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, and 22), and PENDING-DECISIONS.md.
2. Trace each conflicting rule to its local source section. Distinguish reproduced requirements from locally proposed interpretations.
3. Separate:
   - Application-wide administrator authority.
   - Project membership roles.
   - Project creator identity.
   - Ownership, if distinct from creator identity or role.
   - Membership lifecycle/provisioning states.
4. Present a small set of coherent alternatives for Owner/Admin representation. Explain consequences for existing requirements, permission checks, uniqueness/integrity constraints, and future migrations.
5. Recommend an option with explicit reasoning, but do not treat your recommendation as approved.
6. Ask concise questions covering the unresolved choices necessary for a coherent decision:
   - Is Owner a separate role, an ownership relation, or a protected interpretation of Admin?
   - Can ownership change, and how does that interact with immutable creator attribution?
   - Which last-member protections apply, to which roles and membership states?
   - Who may assign/change roles, remove members, or affect the protected owner?
   - How does Application Administrator authority interact with project ownership?
   - Which Owner/Manager/Admin permissions apply to the conflicting project metadata/settings actions?
   - How does PENDING_PROVISIONING transition into active membership?

Do not introduce ownership transfer or any other feature merely because you discuss its implications. “Unsupported in the current scope” is a valid explicit decision.

If existing local records already contain an explicit user-approved decision, cite it and ask only about remaining gaps. Otherwise, pause for my answers before finalizing the decision.

Phase 2 — only after explicit user approval
Create or update a decision record in the prescribed documentation location. If no ADR convention exists, use docs/architecture/control-database-role-decision.md.

Record:
- Decision status and the actual user approval; do not fabricate approval or dates.
- Source conflicts and the selected interpretation.
- Canonical terminology and mappings from conflicting legacy/source labels.
- A permission matrix limited to the actions examined.
- Creator/owner invariants, protected-member rules, and membership lifecycle.
- Effects on future schema constraints versus authorization/use-case logic.
- Rejected alternatives and rationale.
- Remaining questions and precisely which downstream work remains blocked.
- Planned acceptance scenarios, clearly labeled as not implemented or executed.

Update the affected role-related sections of control-database-contracts.md to reference the approved decision. Preserve source traceability and unrelated pending decisions. Do not edit context/ outside relis/.

Verification
- Check that the matrix and invariants are internally consistent.
- Include planned scenarios for forbidden role escalation, cross-project access, protected-member removal/demotion, provisioning failures/retries, and concurrent changes that could remove the last protected member.
- Distinguish database-enforceable constraints from transactional authorization rules.
- Check local links and references.
- No Docker, migrations, builds, or empty test suites are needed for this documentation task.

Completion
Do not mark 03.03 complete while required role decisions remain unapproved. A proposal alone is not completion.

Report the approved decisions, files changed, consistency checks, and remaining blockers. Stop after this sub-issue. Do not implement 03.04/03.05, close the parent issue, export a session, commit, or push.

content.text:
## Phase 1 — Analysis (no decision file created yet; this is analysis only)

I re-checked guides 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 22 and `PENDING-DECISIONS.md` against the baseline/contracts docs already in `docs/architecture/`. Below is the trace, then a small set of coherent alternatives, then the questions I need answered before writing any decision record.

### 1. The five dimensions, separated

| Dimension | Source | What it actually says |
|---|---|---|
| **Application-wide administrator authority** | 13 — Data model/Users&permissions; 15 — Users&permissions ("Application Administrator has audited authority over every... project, and membership") | A `User`-level flag/enum, orthogonal to any project membership. 13: "the final active Application Administrator cannot be archived or demoted." Consistently treated as global, audited, override-everything access across 15/19/21/22 — **this dimension is not actually in conflict anywhere.** |
| **Project membership roles** | 15 — Data model: enum `PROJECT_ADMIN, PROJECT_MANAGER, REVIEWER, VALIDATOR, GUEST` | The only place a role *enum* is literally spelled out. |
| **Project creator identity** | 18 — API behavior: `Project.createdByUserId`, set once at creation, "never accepted from the client"; 19 — Users&permissions: `currentUserId === project.createdByUserId` is the *only* backend check for edit/publish/archive authority | Immutable, single-valued, independent of any enum — a plain foreign key on `Project`. |
| **Ownership, if distinct from creator/role** | 18 — API behavior: "protected `PROJECT_OWNER`... assigned automatically to the creator; cannot be assigned/removed/changed by membership-management endpoints; the backend enforces it corresponds to `Project.createdByUserId`"; 21 — Users&permissions: "Only `PROJECT_OWNER` can access `/settings`" | `PROJECT_OWNER` is used as a **role-gating value** (checked the same way `PROJECT_ADMIN` would be), not as a side-channel flag — see the recommendation below for why this matters. |
| **Membership lifecycle/provisioning states** | 15 — Data model: `ACTIVE, REMOVED`; 18 — API behavior: creator's Owner membership created as `PENDING_PROVISIONING`, "activated... only after the Project DB is available and `v1` has been persisted" | 18 adds a third state 15 never anticipated. |

### 2. The conflict, traced precisely

- **15 already conflates "Owner" and "Admin" in its own prose**, before 18 ever enters the picture: 15 — Users&permissions reads, in order: *"The creator becomes Project Owner when project creation succeeds."* → *"A Project Admin and Project Manager can add, invite, change the role of, and remove users..."* → *"A Project Owner/Manager can assign: Project Manager, Reviewer, Validator, or Guest."* Notice `PROJECT_ADMIN` is **never** in that assignable list — only Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest are assignable. That's a strong internal signal that 15's own author was already treating "Project Owner" and "Project Admin" as the same thing, just inconsistently labeled — not that two independent senior roles exist.
- **16 adds a third label**: "The creator receives a **pending Project Manager** membership in the Control DB" (16 — Users&permissions) — a third name for the same initial-creator-membership concept, reinforcing that no source has ever described *two separate* senior roles (an Admin distinct from an Owner) being held by *different* people.
- **18 formalizes `PROJECT_OWNER`** with real protection semantics 15 never had: immutable correspondence to `createdByUserId`, un-assignable/un-removable via normal membership endpoints, and a `PENDING_PROVISIONING` lifecycle state.
- **21 uses `PROJECT_OWNER` as a literal access-control value** ("Only `PROJECT_OWNER` can access `/settings`"), structurally identical to how 15 would check `PROJECT_ADMIN` — and 21's own UI-behavior "Access rules" paragraph then contradicts its own Users&permissions line by also granting Project Manager four of the five tabs (not General settings). `PENDING-DECISIONS` item 11 already names this as 21's self-contradiction.
- **22 only ever says "Project Admin"** for project-scoped audit/undo access, never "Owner" — and flags in its own Gaps that "Project Admin and Owner require an approved mapping."
- **The last-protected-member guard** is internally split inside 15 alone: Acceptance criteria says "last Project Admin"; API behavior says "last-Project-Manager guard."
- **19 vs. 21** disagree on whether anyone other than Owner+App Admin ever gets metadata/settings access (`PENDING-DECISIONS` items 6 and 11).

None of this is resolved by the two existing documents — `control-database-contracts.md` §5.1/§5.2/§5.5 record exactly these gaps without picking a side, as instructed at the time.

### 3. Coherent alternatives for the central question (Owner representation)

**Option A — Owner replaces Admin.** `PROJECT_OWNER` becomes the sole protected, creator-bound top-tier value; 15's `PROJECT_ADMIN` is read as the same concept under an inconsistent earlier label and is renamed. `PROJECT_MANAGER` remains the highest *ordinary* (assignable, removable) role. Consequence: the enum has 5 values (`PROJECT_OWNER, PROJECT_MANAGER, REVIEWER, VALIDATOR, GUEST`), owner is 1-per-project by construction (FK-backed), and most of the "last Admin vs last Manager" conflict dissolves — there is nothing to "remove" for Owner since membership endpoints can never touch it at all.

**Option B — Owner above Admin.** Add `PROJECT_OWNER` as a new 6th, protected value sitting above an *unchanged* `PROJECT_ADMIN`. Consequence: preserves 15's enum literally, but requires inventing a delegated-Admin concept that **no source ever describes being assigned to anyone other than the creator** — every single mention of "Project Admin" across 13/15/16/18/19/21/22 is either ambiguous-with-Owner or generic-for-whoever-holds-the-top-role. This option manufactures a role with no described assignment path.

**Option C — Owner as a derived attribute, not a role.** Keep 15's five-value enum as the *only* role enum; represent ownership purely via `Project.createdByUserId` plus a protection flag, with no `PROJECT_OWNER` enum value anywhere. Consequence: directly contradicts 21's and 18's literal, repeated use of `PROJECT_OWNER` as something checked the same way a role is checked ("Only `PROJECT_OWNER` can access..."), and contradicts 18's statement that the Owner membership has its own lifecycle state (`PENDING_PROVISIONING`) — a plain derived attribute wouldn't need a membership-row lifecycle at all.

**My recommendation: Option A.** It requires inventing nothing, it directly resolves 15's own internal "Owner"/"Admin" conflation (found in §2 above) rather than treating it as a lasting institution, and it matches 18/21's much more detailed and more recently-elaborated protection semantics literally. I am **not** treating this as approved — it is a recommendation pending your decision, per this task's explicit instruction.

### 4. What I am *not* asking about (already explicit, or correctly out of scope)

- **App Administrator vs. ownership**: already consistent everywhere (global, audited, orthogonal to membership) — no question needed.
- **Who may assign/remove roles**: 15 already specifies this precisely (Owner/Manager assign Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest; Manager cannot remove Admin/Owner) — no question needed.
- **PENDING_PROVISIONING → active transition**: 18 already states this precisely (activates only after Project DB ready *and* `v1` persisted) — no question needed.
- **Ownership transfer as a feature**: no source describes it. Per this task's own instruction, "unsupported in the current scope" is a valid explicit answer — I'm asking only to confirm that, not proposing to build it.

I need your decisions on the four genuinely open forks below before I write anything to `docs/architecture/control-database-role-decision.md`.

questions.question: How should the protected project-creator role (PROJECT_OWNER, per guide 18) relate to guide 15's PROJECT_ADMIN enum value?

options.label: Owner replaces Admin (Recommended)
options.description: PROJECT_OWNER becomes the sole protected top-tier role, renamed from 15's PROJECT_ADMIN. PROJECT_MANAGER remains the highest ordinary assignable role. Matches 15's own prose, which already uses 'Project Owner' and 'Project Admin' interchangeably, and matches 18/21's detailed, literal protected-role checks.

options.label: Owner above Admin
options.description: Add PROJECT_OWNER as a new protected 6th role sitting above an unchanged PROJECT_ADMIN. Preserves 15's enum as-is, but requires a delegated 'Admin' role no source ever describes being assigned to anyone other than the creator.

options.label: Owner as an attribute, not a role
options.description: Keep 15's five-value role enum as the only role enum. Represent ownership purely as Project.createdByUserId plus a protection flag on the membership row - no PROJECT_OWNER value in the role enum at all. Contradicts 18/21's literal, repeated treatment of PROJECT_OWNER as a role-gating value with its own membership lifecycle state.

questions.question: Guide 15 conflicts internally on protecting the 'last Project Admin' vs. the 'last Project Manager' from removal. Given Owner will be a single, permanently protected, creator-bound role under any option above, should removal of the last Project Manager also be blocked?

options.label: No Manager guard needed (Recommended)
options.description: Only the Owner is permanently protected (and the Owner can never be removed via membership endpoints at all, under any option above). # Project role/ownership decision — `PROJECT_OWNER` vs. `PROJECT_ADMIN`

Local sub-issue: [03.03 — Resolve the PROJECT_OWNER/PROJECT_ADMIN discrepancy
before finalizing identity and membership enums and
constraints](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md), under parent
[03 — Create control Prisma schema](../../../context/notion-tasks/03-control-prisma.md).

No `docs/adr/` convention exists in this checkout (confirmed empty/absent
before writing this file), so this record uses the fallback location named
by the sub-issue's own instructions.

## 1. Status and approval

**Status: Decided.** This record documents four decisions the user
explicitly approved in this session, each by selecting the recommended
option presented via a structured question (`AskUserQuestion`), after being
shown the sourced analysis and alternatives below. No decision in this
record is a Claude recommendation standing alone — every one carries
explicit user approval, recorded per-decision in §3.

This decision is scoped **narrowly** to the `PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN`
representation, the associated protected-member rule, ownership-transfer
support, and the Settings/metadata permission split named by this
sub-issue's own question list. It does **not** resolve every open item in
[`control-database-contracts.md`](control-database-contracts.md)'s §5 — see
§8 for exactly which gates this decision does and does not close.

## 2. Source conflicts (traced, not re-litigated)

Full citations already exist in [`control-database-contracts.md`](control-database-contracts.md)
§5.1/§5.2/§5.5 and [`PENDING-DECISIONS.md`](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md)
item 2; this section adds the specific textual evidence that shaped the
selected interpretation, re-verified against the guides during this
sub-issue:

- **15 already conflates "Owner" and "Admin" in its own prose**, before 18
  enters the picture. 15 — Users and permissions reads, in sequence: *"The
  creator becomes Project Owner when project creation succeeds."* → *"A
  Project Admin and Project Manager can add, invite, change the role of, and
  remove users..."* → *"A Project Owner/Manager can assign: Project Manager,
  Reviewer, Validator, or Guest."* `PROJECT_ADMIN` never appears in that
  assignable list — only Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest do. This is
  internal evidence that 15's own author already treated "Project Owner"
  and "Project Admin" as one concept under two labels.
- **16 — Users and permissions** adds a third label for the same
  initial-creator-membership concept: *"The creator receives a **pending
  Project Manager** membership in the Control DB."*
- **18 — API behavior** formalizes `PROJECT_OWNER` with protection semantics
  15 never had: *"assigned automatically to the creator; cannot be
  assigned/removed/changed by membership-management endpoints; the backend
  enforces it corresponds to `Project.createdByUserId`"*, plus a
  `PENDING_PROVISIONING` membership lifecycle state.
- **21 — Users and permissions** uses `PROJECT_OWNER` as a literal
  access-control value (*"Only `PROJECT_OWNER` can access `/settings`"*),
  structurally identical to how 15 would check a role — then 21's own UI
  behavior "Access rules" paragraph contradicts that same sentence by also
  granting Project Manager four of the five Settings tabs.
- **22** only ever says "Project Admin" for project-scoped audit/undo
  access, never "Owner," and its own Gaps section flags that "Project Admin
  and Owner require an approved mapping."
- **15's last-protected-member guard is internally split**: Acceptance
  criteria says "Removing the last Project Admin is rejected"; API behavior
  says the add-member flow checks "the last-Project-Manager guard."
- **19 vs. 21** disagree on whether Project Manager ever gets
  project-administration access beyond ordinary project-scoped work
  (`PENDING-DECISIONS` items 6 and 11).

## 3. Decisions (each user-approved)

### 3.1 Owner representation — **Owner replaces Admin**

`PROJECT_OWNER` is the sole protected, creator-bound top-tier project role.
15's `PROJECT_ADMIN` enum value is renamed to `PROJECT_OWNER` — it is not a
second, separate senior role. `PROJECT_MANAGER` remains the highest
*ordinary* (assignable, removable) role below it.

**Canonical role enum:** `PROJECT_OWNER, PROJECT_MANAGER, REVIEWER,
VALIDATOR, GUEST` (five values — same count as 15's original list, with
`PROJECT_ADMIN` renamed, not a value added).

*Rejected alternatives* (presented, not chosen):
- *Owner above Admin* — would add `PROJECT_OWNER` as a 6th value sitting
  above an unchanged `PROJECT_ADMIN`. Rejected because no source describes a
  delegated "Admin" ever assigned to anyone other than the creator; this
  would manufacture a role with no described assignment path.
- *Owner as a derived attribute, not a role* — would keep 15's five-value
  enum untouched and represent ownership only via `Project.createdByUserId`
  plus a flag. Rejected because 18/21 use `PROJECT_OWNER` as a literal
  role-gating value with its own membership lifecycle state
  (`PENDING_PROVISIONING`), which a plain derived attribute would not need.

### 3.2 Last-protected-member guard — **no Manager-count guard**

Only the Owner is permanently protected, and that protection is absolute,
not count-based: the Owner membership can **never** be removed or
role-changed through any membership-management endpoint, regardless of how
many other members exist (see §5). There is **no** "at least one Manager
must remain" rule — Project Managers (and every other non-Owner role) can
be removed down to zero; the Owner alone can always re-add one.

This supersedes both halves of 15's internal conflict: "last Project Admin"
(Acceptance criteria) is read as describing the Owner's now-absolute
protection; "last-Project-Manager guard" (API behavior) is explicitly
**rejected** as a real, independent invariant — 15's own text at that
specific point should be read as superseded by this decision, not as a
requirement still pending implementation.

*Rejected alternative:* requiring at least one Project Manager at all
times. Rejected because no use case in any read guide depends on a Manager
always being present — the Owner's unconditional protection already
guarantees the project is always administrable, and adding a
quantity-based guard for Manager alone would introduce a validation rule no
source actually needs.

### 3.3 Ownership transfer — **not supported**

`Project.createdByUserId` and the Owner's `Membership` row are permanently,
immutably bound 1:1 to the original creator. No code path, use case, or
schema relation will support reassigning the Owner membership to a
different user. This is the explicit "unsupported in current scope" answer
this sub-issue's own instructions permit, not an oversight.

*Rejected alternatives:* designing a separate, reassignable owner relation
"for later," or leaving the question open. Both rejected because no source
guide describes a transfer feature, and per [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md)'s
working agreement, this repository does not design for hypothetical future
requirements that no approved specification names.

### 3.4 Settings/metadata permission split — **Owner + Application Administrator only, everywhere**

For every action named in 19 (project metadata: title/description/research
questions edit, publish/unpublish, archive/restore) and every Settings tab
in 21 (General, Screening, Quality Assessment, Data Extraction, Reporting):
only `PROJECT_OWNER` and Application Administrator have access. Project
Manager has **none** of this access, in any tab.

This selects 19's and 21's own stricter "Users and permissions" wording
literally, and **explicitly overrides** 21's own looser UI-behavior "Access
rules" paragraph, which had granted Project Manager four of the five
Settings tabs. When 21 is eventually implemented, that specific UI-behavior
sentence must be treated as superseded by this decision, not implemented as
written.

*Rejected alternative:* granting Project Manager delegated access to
Screening/QA/Data-extraction/Reporting settings (21's own UI-behavior
reading). Rejected in favor of the stricter, internally consistent reading
shared by 19 and 21's "Users and permissions" sections, rather than 21's
self-contradicting UI-behavior text.

## 4. Canonical terminology — mapping from every conflicting source label

| Source label (as written) | Where it appears | Canonical meaning after this decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROJECT_ADMIN` (role enum) | 15 — Data model | Renamed to `PROJECT_OWNER` |
| "Project Owner" (prose) | 15 — Users and permissions | `PROJECT_OWNER` (unchanged meaning, now also the enum value) |
| "pending Project Manager membership" (for the creator) | 16 — Users and permissions | The creator's initial membership is `PROJECT_OWNER` with status `PENDING_PROVISIONING` — **not** `PROJECT_MANAGER`. 16's label is superseded by 18's more detailed, later-formalized contract. |
| `PROJECT_OWNER` | 18 — API behavior; 21 — Users and permissions | Canonical, unchanged |
| "Project Admin" (in an audit/undo context) | 22 — Users and permissions | `PROJECT_OWNER` |
| "last Project Admin" (guard) | 15 — Acceptance criteria | The Owner's unconditional, non-count-based protection (§3.2) |
| "last-Project-Manager guard" | 15 — API behavior | **Rejected** — no such guard exists (§3.2) |
| "Project Manager... Screening/QA/Extraction/Reporting access" | 21 — UI behavior ("Access rules") | **Superseded** — Manager has no Settings access of any kind (§3.4) |

## 5. Permission matrix (limited to the actions examined by this decision)

Legend: ✅ allowed · ❌ forbidden · n/a not applicable to that role.
Application Administrator rows assume its existing "audited global access"
(13, 15) — every ✅ for Application Administrator is an **audited** action,
per the sources already cited in `control-database-contracts.md` §3.1/§3.8.

| Action | Owner | Manager | Reviewer | Validator | Guest | App Admin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Add/invite a member (assign Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (any project) |
| Assign the `PROJECT_OWNER` role to anyone | ❌ (no such action exists) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ (no such action exists — §3.3) |
| Change another member's role (to Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Remove a member (Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Remove or role-change the `PROJECT_OWNER` membership | ❌ (not even by itself) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ (no path exists — §3.3) |
| View Team page (active members + invitations) | ✅ | ✅ | *unspecified — see §8* | *unspecified — see §8* | *unspecified — see §8* | ✅ |
| Open workspace (any active member) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (audited) |
| Edit project metadata / publish/unpublish / archive/restore (19) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| General settings tab (21) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Screening / QA / Data-extraction / Reporting settings tabs (21) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| View project audit events / undo centre, own project (22) | ✅ | ❌ (no delegated grant mechanism designed here) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (any project) |

Rows marked "unspecified" are **not** decided by this sub-issue — they were
not among the seven questions this sub-issue's own instructions listed, and
no source states them either way. They are carried forward as an open,
low-severity gap in §8, not silently defaulted.

## 6. Creator/owner invariants, protected-member rules, membership lifecycle

- **Exactly one `PROJECT_OWNER` membership per project, always.** Created in
  the same Control DB transaction as the `Project` row itself (18 — API
  behavior), so a project is never without one and never has more than one.
- **`Project.createdByUserId` is immutable**, set once at creation, never
  accepted from the client (18, 19).
- **Structural correspondence**: the `PROJECT_OWNER` membership's `userId`
  for a given project always equals that project's `createdByUserId` — this
  is a standing invariant, not merely true at creation time, since no
  transfer path exists (§3.3).
- **Membership status enum**: `PENDING_PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, REMOVED`.
  `PENDING_PROVISIONING` applies only to the Owner's membership, only
  between project-creation and the moment the Project DB is ready **and**
  protocol `v1` is persisted (18 — API behavior); every other membership
  (added via Team, or via invitation acceptance) is created directly
  `ACTIVE` (15 — API behavior).
- **The Owner membership never reaches `REMOVED`** through any
  membership-management endpoint, by anyone, including Application
  Administrator (§3.3 — no reassignment/removal path was ever described).
  Archiving a *project* (19) is a separate, `Project`-level state change and
  does not remove the Owner's membership row.
- **Every other role's membership can reach `REMOVED` with no count floor**
  (§3.2) — a project may validly have zero Managers, zero Reviewers, etc.,
  at any time; only the Owner's presence is guaranteed.
- **Manager cannot remove or role-change the Owner** — now a redundant
  restatement of the absolute rule above, since *nobody* can, not a
  Manager-specific restriction.

## 7. Effects on future schema constraints vs. authorization/use-case logic

This decision does not implement anything (03.04/03.05's job), but it does
determine which of the rules above are database-enforceable constraints
versus application-layer (authorization/use-case) logic that 03.04/03.05
must still write in code:

**Database-enforceable (Prisma/PostgreSQL), for 03.04 to design:**
- `Membership.role` enum includes `PROJECT_OWNER` (replacing
  `PROJECT_ADMIN`), `PROJECT_MANAGER`, `REVIEWER`, `VALIDATOR`, `GUEST`.
- `Membership.status` enum includes `PENDING_PROVISIONING`, `ACTIVE`,
  `REMOVED`.
- A uniqueness constraint ensuring at most one `PROJECT_OWNER` membership
  per project (e.g., a partial unique index on `projectId` where
  `role = 'PROJECT_OWNER'`, or an equivalent 1:1 structural guarantee) —
  this is the one genuinely new DB-level constraint introduced by this
  decision; its exact mechanism is a 03.04 implementation choice, not fixed
  here.
- The existing `(projectId, userId)` active-membership uniqueness
  (unchanged from `control-database-contracts.md` §3.4).

**Not database-enforceable — must be written as authorization/use-case
logic:**
- The `PROJECT_OWNER` membership's `userId` always equals
  `Project.createdByUserId`: PostgreSQL cannot natively express "this FK's
  target equals that other table's column" as a simple constraint. 03.04
  may choose to reinforce this with a trigger, but at minimum it must be
  enforced at creation time in application code and never mutated
  afterward — this document does not choose a trigger vs. pure-application
  enforcement for 03.04.
- "Owner can never be assigned/removed/role-changed via membership
  endpoints" — the database would technically permit an `UPDATE` to that
  row; this must be a hard rejection in the membership-management use-case
  layer, not a schema-level block.
- "No Manager-count guard" — the **absence** of a rule: 03.04/03.05 must
  specifically **not** add a count-based rejection for removing the last
  Manager (an easy mistake to copy from 15's literal text without this
  decision).
- Settings/metadata tab authorization (Owner + Application Administrator
  only) — a pure API-boundary role check, not expressible as a schema
  constraint.
- `PENDING_PROVISIONING` → `ACTIVE` transition timing, gated on Project DB
  readiness **and** `v1` persistence (18) — workflow/orchestration logic.

## 8. Remaining questions and precisely what remains blocked

**Explicitly NOT resolved by this decision** (still open in
`control-database-contracts.md` §5, unaffected by anything above):

- **§5.4 — who may create a project at all** (any authenticated user vs. a
  named "creation permission"). This decision only concerns the
  representation/protection of the role *after* a project exists — it does
  not decide who may start one.
- **§5.7 — Project DB connection-mapping storage** (unrelated gap).
- **§5.9 — cross-project audit correlation mechanism** (unrelated gap).
- **§5.10 — draft-to-Project conversion disposition** (unrelated gap).
- **§5.8 — invitation-validity-period storage location** (unrelated gap).
- **22's "Project Manager... limited rights must be explicitly granted in

# Project role/ownership decision — `PROJECT_OWNER` vs. `PROJECT_ADMIN`

Local sub-issue: [03.03 — Resolve the PROJECT_OWNER/PROJECT_ADMIN discrepancy
before finalizing identity and membership enums and
constraints](../../../context/notion-tasks/sub-issues/03-03.md), under parent
[03 — Create control Prisma schema](../../../context/notion-tasks/03-control-prisma.md).

No `docs/adr/` convention exists in this checkout (confirmed empty/absent
before writing this file), so this record uses the fallback location named
by the sub-issue's own instructions.

## 1. Status and approval

**Status: Decided.** This record documents four decisions the user
explicitly approved in this session, each by selecting the recommended
option presented via a structured question (`AskUserQuestion`), after being
shown the sourced analysis and alternatives below. No decision in this
record is a Claude recommendation standing alone — every one carries
explicit user approval, recorded per-decision in §3.

This decision is scoped **narrowly** to the `PROJECT_OWNER`/`PROJECT_ADMIN`
representation, the associated protected-member rule, ownership-transfer
support, and the Settings/metadata permission split named by this
sub-issue's own question list. It does **not** resolve every open item in
[`control-database-contracts.md`](control-database-contracts.md)'s §5 — see
§8 for exactly which gates this decision does and does not close.

## 2. Source conflicts (traced, not re-litigated)

Full citations already exist in [`control-database-contracts.md`](control-database-contracts.md)
§5.1/§5.2/§5.5 and [`PENDING-DECISIONS.md`](../../../context/notion-tasks/PENDING-DECISIONS.md)
item 2; this section adds the specific textual evidence that shaped the
selected interpretation, re-verified against the guides during this
sub-issue:

- **15 already conflates "Owner" and "Admin" in its own prose**, before 18
  enters the picture. 15 — Users and permissions reads, in sequence: *"The
  creator becomes Project Owner when project creation succeeds."* → *"A
  Project Admin and Project Manager can add, invite, change the role of, and
  remove users..."* → *"A Project Owner/Manager can assign: Project Manager,
  Reviewer, Validator, or Guest."* `PROJECT_ADMIN` never appears in that
  assignable list — only Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest do. This is
  internal evidence that 15's own author already treated "Project Owner"
  and "Project Admin" as one concept under two labels.
- **16 — Users and permissions** adds a third label for the same
  initial-creator-membership concept: *"The creator receives a **pending
  Project Manager** membership in the Control DB."*
- **18 — API behavior** formalizes `PROJECT_OWNER` with protection semantics
  15 never had: *"assigned automatically to the creator; cannot be
  assigned/removed/changed by membership-management endpoints; the backend
  enforces it corresponds to `Project.createdByUserId`"*, plus a
  `PENDING_PROVISIONING` membership lifecycle state.
- **21 — Users and permissions** uses `PROJECT_OWNER` as a literal
  access-control value (*"Only `PROJECT_OWNER` can access `/settings`"*),
  structurally identical to how 15 would check a role — then 21's own UI
  behavior "Access rules" paragraph contradicts that same sentence by also
  granting Project Manager four of the five Settings tabs.
- **22** only ever says "Project Admin" for project-scoped audit/undo
  access, never "Owner," and its own Gaps section flags that "Project Admin
  and Owner require an approved mapping."
- **15's last-protected-member guard is internally split**: Acceptance
  criteria says "Removing the last Project Admin is rejected"; API behavior
  says the add-member flow checks "the last-Project-Manager guard."
- **19 vs. 21** disagree on whether Project Manager ever gets
  project-administration access beyond ordinary project-scoped work
  (`PENDING-DECISIONS` items 6 and 11).

## 3. Decisions (each user-approved)

### 3.1 Owner representation — **Owner replaces Admin**

`PROJECT_OWNER` is the sole protected, creator-bound top-tier project role.
15's `PROJECT_ADMIN` enum value is renamed to `PROJECT_OWNER` — it is not a
second, separate senior role. `PROJECT_MANAGER` remains the highest
*ordinary* (assignable, removable) role below it.

**Canonical role enum:** `PROJECT_OWNER, PROJECT_MANAGER, REVIEWER,
VALIDATOR, GUEST` (five values — same count as 15's original list, with
`PROJECT_ADMIN` renamed, not a value added).

*Rejected alternatives* (presented, not chosen):
- *Owner above Admin* — would add `PROJECT_OWNER` as a 6th value sitting
  above an unchanged `PROJECT_ADMIN`. Rejected because no source describes a
  delegated "Admin" ever assigned to anyone other than the creator; this
  would manufacture a role with no described assignment path.
- *Owner as a derived attribute, not a role* — would keep 15's five-value
  enum untouched and represent ownership only via `Project.createdByUserId`
  plus a flag. Rejected because 18/21 use `PROJECT_OWNER` as a literal
  role-gating value with its own membership lifecycle state
  (`PENDING_PROVISIONING`), which a plain derived attribute would not need.

### 3.2 Last-protected-member guard — **no Manager-count guard**

Only the Owner is permanently protected, and that protection is absolute,
not count-based: the Owner membership can **never** be removed or
role-changed through any membership-management endpoint, regardless of how
many other members exist (see §5). There is **no** "at least one Manager
must remain" rule — Project Managers (and every other non-Owner role) can
be removed down to zero; the Owner alone can always re-add one.

This supersedes both halves of 15's internal conflict: "last Project Admin"
(Acceptance criteria) is read as describing the Owner's now-absolute
protection; "last-Project-Manager guard" (API behavior) is explicitly
**rejected** as a real, independent invariant — 15's own text at that
specific point should be read as superseded by this decision, not as a
requirement still pending implementation.

*Rejected alternative:* requiring at least one Project Manager at all
times. Rejected because no use case in any read guide depends on a Manager
always being present — the Owner's unconditional protection already
guarantees the project is always administrable, and adding a
quantity-based guard for Manager alone would introduce a validation rule no
source actually needs.

### 3.3 Ownership transfer — **not supported**

`Project.createdByUserId` and the Owner's `Membership` row are permanently,
immutably bound 1:1 to the original creator. No code path, use case, or
schema relation will support reassigning the Owner membership to a
different user. This is the explicit "unsupported in current scope" answer
this sub-issue's own instructions permit, not an oversight.

*Rejected alternatives:* designing a separate, reassignable owner relation
"for later," or leaving the question open. Both rejected because no source
guide describes a transfer feature, and per [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md)'s
working agreement, this repository does not design for hypothetical future
requirements that no approved specification names.

### 3.4 Settings/metadata permission split — **Owner + Application Administrator only, everywhere**

For every action named in 19 (project metadata: title/description/research
questions edit, publish/unpublish, archive/restore) and every Settings tab
in 21 (General, Screening, Quality Assessment, Data Extraction, Reporting):
only `PROJECT_OWNER` and Application Administrator have access. Project
Manager has **none** of this access, in any tab.

This selects 19's and 21's own stricter "Users and permissions" wording
literally, and **explicitly overrides** 21's own looser UI-behavior "Access
rules" paragraph, which had granted Project Manager four of the five
Settings tabs. When 21 is eventually implemented, that specific UI-behavior
sentence must be treated as superseded by this decision, not implemented as
written.

*Rejected alternative:* granting Project Manager delegated access to
Screening/QA/Data-extraction/Reporting settings (21's own UI-behavior
reading). Rejected in favor of the stricter, internally consistent reading
shared by 19 and 21's "Users and permissions" sections, rather than 21's
self-contradicting UI-behavior text.

## 4. Canonical terminology — mapping from every conflicting source label

| Source label (as written) | Where it appears | Canonical meaning after this decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROJECT_ADMIN` (role enum) | 15 — Data model | Renamed to `PROJECT_OWNER` |
| "Project Owner" (prose) | 15 — Users and permissions | `PROJECT_OWNER` (unchanged meaning, now also the enum value) |
| "pending Project Manager membership" (for the creator) | 16 — Users and permissions | The creator's initial membership is `PROJECT_OWNER` with status `PENDING_PROVISIONING` — **not** `PROJECT_MANAGER`. 16's label is superseded by 18's more detailed, later-formalized contract. |
| `PROJECT_OWNER` | 18 — API behavior; 21 — Users and permissions | Canonical, unchanged |
| "Project Admin" (in an audit/undo context) | 22 — Users and permissions | `PROJECT_OWNER` |
| "last Project Admin" (guard) | 15 — Acceptance criteria | The Owner's unconditional, non-count-based protection (§3.2) |
| "last-Project-Manager guard" | 15 — API behavior | **Rejected** — no such guard exists (§3.2) |
| "Project Manager... Screening/QA/Extraction/Reporting access" | 21 — UI behavior ("Access rules") | **Superseded** — Manager has no Settings access of any kind (§3.4) |

## 5. Permission matrix (limited to the actions examined by this decision)

Legend: ✅ allowed · ❌ forbidden · n/a not applicable to that role.
Application Administrator rows assume its existing "audited global access"
(13, 15) — every ✅ for Application Administrator is an **audited** action,
per the sources already cited in `control-database-contracts.md` §3.1/§3.8.

| Action | Owner | Manager | Reviewer | Validator | Guest | App Admin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Add/invite a member (assign Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (any project) |
| Assign the `PROJECT_OWNER` role to anyone | ❌ (no such action exists) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ (no such action exists — §3.3) |
| Change another member's role (to Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Remove a member (Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Remove or role-change the `PROJECT_OWNER` membership | ❌ (not even by itself) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ (no path exists — §3.3) |
| View Team page (active members + invitations) | ✅ | ✅ | *unspecified — see §8* | *unspecified — see §8* | *unspecified — see §8* | ✅ |
| Open workspace (any active member) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (audited) |
| Edit project metadata / publish/unpublish / archive/restore (19) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| General settings tab (21) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Screening / QA / Data-extraction / Reporting settings tabs (21) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| View project audit events / undo centre, own project (22) | ✅ | ❌ (no delegated grant mechanism designed here) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (any project) |

Rows marked "unspecified" are **not** decided by this sub-issue — they were
not among the seven questions this sub-issue's own instructions listed, and
no source states them either way. They are carried forward as an open,
low-severity gap in §8, not silently defaulted.

## 6. Creator/owner invariants, protected-member rules, membership lifecycle

- **Exactly one `PROJECT_OWNER` membership per project, always.** Created in
  the same Control DB transaction as the `Project` row itself (18 — API
  behavior), so a project is never without one and never has more than one.
- **`Project.createdByUserId` is immutable**, set once at creation, never
  accepted from the client (18, 19).
- **Structural correspondence**: the `PROJECT_OWNER` membership's `userId`
  for a given project always equals that project's `createdByUserId` — this
  is a standing invariant, not merely true at creation time, since no
  transfer path exists (§3.3).
- **Membership status enum**: `PENDING_PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, REMOVED`.
  `PENDING_PROVISIONING` applies only to the Owner's membership, only
  between project-creation and the moment the Project DB is ready **and**
  protocol `v1` is persisted (18 — API behavior); every other membership
  (added via Team, or via invitation acceptance) is created directly
  `ACTIVE` (15 — API behavior).
- **The Owner membership never reaches `REMOVED`** through any
  membership-management endpoint, by anyone, including Application
  Administrator (§3.3 — no reassignment/removal path was ever described).
  Archiving a *project* (19) is a separate, `Project`-level state change and
  does not remove the Owner's membership row.
- **Every other role's membership can reach `REMOVED` with no count floor**
  (§3.2) — a project may validly have zero Managers, zero Reviewers, etc.,
  at any time; only the Owner's presence is guaranteed.
- **Manager cannot remove or role-change the Owner** — now a redundant
  restatement of the absolute rule above, since *nobody* can, not a
  Manager-specific restriction.

This decision does not implement anything (03.04/03.05's job), but it does
determine which of the rules above are database-enforceable constraints
versus application-layer (authorization/use-case) logic that 03.04/03.05
must still write in code:

- `Membership.role` enum includes `PROJECT_OWNER` (replacing

- `Membership.status` enum includes `PENDING_PROVISIONING`, `ACTIVE`,
  `REMOVED`.
- A uniqueness constraint ensuring at most one `PROJECT_OWNER` membership
  per project (e.g., a partial unique index on `projectId` where
  `role = 'PROJECT_OWNER'`, or an equivalent 1:1 structural guarantee) —
  this is the one genuinely new DB-level constraint introduced by this
  decision; its exact mechanism is a 03.04 implementation choice, not fixed
  here.

  (unchanged from `control-database-contracts.md` §3.4).

**Not database-enforceable — must be written as authorization/use-case
logic:**
- The `PROJECT_OWNER` membership's `userId` always equals
  `Project.createdByUserId`: PostgreSQL cannot natively express "this FK's
  target equals that other table's column" as a simple constraint. 03.04
  may choose to reinforce this with a trigger, but at minimum it must be
  enforced at creation time in application code and never mutated
  afterward — this document does not choose a trigger vs. pure-application
  enforcement for 03.04.

  endpoints" — the database would technically permit an `UPDATE` to that
  row; this must be a hard rejection in the membership-management use-case
  layer, not a schema-level block.

  specifically **not** add a count-based rejection for removing the last
  Manager (an easy mistake to copy from 15's literal text without this
  decision).
- Settings/metadata tab authorization (Owner + Application Administrator
  only) — a pure API-boundary role check, not expressible as a schema
  constraint.
- `PENDING_PROVISIONING` → `ACTIVE` transition timing, gated on Project DB

  15 never had: *"assigned automatically to the creator; cannot be
  assigned/removed/changed by membership-management endpoints; the backend
  enforces it corresponds to `Project.createdByUserId`"*, plus a
  `PENDING_PROVISIONING` membership lifecycle state.
- **21 — Users and permissions** uses `PROJECT_OWNER` as a literal
  access-control value (*"Only `PROJECT_OWNER` can access `/settings`"*),
  structurally identical to how 15 would check a role — then 21's own UI
  behavior "Access rules" paragraph contradicts that same sentence by also
  granting Project Manager four of the five Settings tabs.
- **22** only ever says "Project Admin" for project-scoped audit/undo
  access, never "Owner," and its own Gaps section flags that "Project Admin
  and Owner require an approved mapping."
- **15's last-protected-member guard is internally split**: Acceptance
  criteria says "Removing the last Project Admin is rejected"; API behavior
  says the add-member flow checks "the last-Project-Manager guard."
- **19 vs. 21** disagree on whether Project Manager ever gets
  project-administration access beyond ordinary project-scoped work
  (`PENDING-DECISIONS` items 6 and 11).

## 3. Decisions (each user-approved)

### 3.1 Owner representation — **Owner replaces Admin**

`PROJECT_OWNER` is the sole protected, creator-bound top-tier project role.
15's `PROJECT_ADMIN` enum value is renamed to `PROJECT_OWNER` — it is not a
second, separate senior role. `PROJECT_MANAGER` remains the highest
*ordinary* (assignable, removable) role below it.

**Canonical role enum:** `PROJECT_OWNER, PROJECT_MANAGER, REVIEWER,
VALIDATOR, GUEST` (five values — same count as 15's original list, with
`PROJECT_ADMIN` renamed, not a value added).

*Rejected alternatives* (presented, not chosen):
- *Owner above Admin* — would add `PROJECT_OWNER` as a 6th value sitting
  above an unchanged `PROJECT_ADMIN`. Rejected because no source describes a
  delegated "Admin" ever assigned to anyone other than the creator; this
  would manufacture a role with no described assignment path.
- *Owner as a derived attribute, not a role* — would keep 15's five-value
  enum untouched and represent ownership only via `Project.createdByUserId`
  plus a flag. Rejected because 18/21 use `PROJECT_OWNER` as a literal
  role-gating value with its own membership lifecycle state
  (`PENDING_PROVISIONING`), which a plain derived attribute would not need.

### 3.2 Last-protected-member guard — **no Manager-count guard**

Only the Owner is permanently protected, and that protection is absolute,
not count-based: the Owner membership can **never** be removed or
role-changed through any membership-management endpoint, regardless of how
many other members exist (see §5). There is **no** "at least one Manager
must remain" rule — Project Managers (and every other non-Owner role) can
be removed down to zero; the Owner alone can always re-add one.

This supersedes both halves of 15's internal conflict: "last Project Admin"
(Acceptance criteria) is read as describing the Owner's now-absolute
protection; "last-Project-Manager guard" (API behavior) is explicitly
**rejected** as a real, independent invariant — 15's own text at that
specific point should be read as superseded by this decision, not as a
requirement still pending implementation.

*Rejected alternative:* requiring at least one Project Manager at all
times. Rejected because no use case in any read guide depends on a Manager
always being present — the Owner's unconditional protection already
guarantees the project is always administrable, and adding a
quantity-based guard for Manager alone would introduce a validation rule no
source actually needs.

### 3.3 Ownership transfer — **not supported**

`Project.createdByUserId` and the Owner's `Membership` row are permanently,
immutably bound 1:1 to the original creator. No code path, use case, or
schema relation will support reassigning the Owner membership to a
different user. This is the explicit "unsupported in current scope" answer
this sub-issue's own instructions permit, not an oversight.

*Rejected alternatives:* designing a separate, reassignable owner relation
"for later," or leaving the question open. Both rejected because no source
guide describes a transfer feature, and per [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md)'s
working agreement, this repository does not design for hypothetical future
requirements that no approved specification names.

### 3.4 Settings/metadata permission split — **Owner + Application Administrator only, everywhere**

For every action named in 19 (project metadata: title/description/research
questions edit, publish/unpublish, archive/restore) and every Settings tab
in 21 (General, Screening, Quality Assessment, Data Extraction, Reporting):
only `PROJECT_OWNER` and Application Administrator have access. Project
Manager has **none** of this access, in any tab.

This selects 19's and 21's own stricter "Users and permissions" wording
literally, and **explicitly overrides** 21's own looser UI-behavior "Access
rules" paragraph, which had granted Project Manager four of the five
Settings tabs. When 21 is eventually implemented, that specific UI-behavior
sentence must be treated as superseded by this decision, not implemented as
written.

*Rejected alternative:* granting Project Manager delegated access to
Screening/QA/Data-extraction/Reporting settings (21's own UI-behavior
reading). Rejected in favor of the stricter, internally consistent reading
shared by 19 and 21's "Users and permissions" sections, rather than 21's
self-contradicting UI-behavior text.

## 4. Canonical terminology — mapping from every conflicting source label

| Source label (as written) | Where it appears | Canonical meaning after this decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROJECT_ADMIN` (role enum) | 15 — Data model | Renamed to `PROJECT_OWNER` |
| "Project Owner" (prose) | 15 — Users and permissions | `PROJECT_OWNER` (unchanged meaning, now also the enum value) |
| "pending Project Manager membership" (for the creator) | 16 — Users and permissions | The creator's initial membership is `PROJECT_OWNER` with status `PENDING_PROVISIONING` — **not** `PROJECT_MANAGER`. 16's label is superseded by 18's more detailed, later-formalized contract. |
| `PROJECT_OWNER` | 18 — API behavior; 21 — Users and permissions | Canonical, unchanged |
| "Project Admin" (in an audit/undo context) | 22 — Users and permissions | `PROJECT_OWNER` |
| "last Project Admin" (guard) | 15 — Acceptance criteria | The Owner's unconditional, non-count-based protection (§3.2) |
| "last-Project-Manager guard" | 15 — API behavior | **Rejected** — no such guard exists (§3.2) |
| "Project Manager... Screening/QA/Extraction/Reporting access" | 21 — UI behavior ("Access rules") | **Superseded** — Manager has no Settings access of any kind (§3.4) |

## 5. Permission matrix (limited to the actions examined by this decision)

Legend: ✅ allowed · ❌ forbidden · n/a not applicable to that role.
Application Administrator rows assume its existing "audited global access"
(13, 15) — every ✅ for Application Administrator is an **audited** action,
per the sources already cited in `control-database-contracts.md` §3.1/§3.8.

| Action | Owner | Manager | Reviewer | Validator | Guest | App Admin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Add/invite a member (assign Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (any project) |
| Assign the `PROJECT_OWNER` role to anyone | ❌ (no such action exists) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ (no such action exists — §3.3) |
| Change another member's role (to Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Remove a member (Manager/Reviewer/Validator/Guest) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Remove or role-change the `PROJECT_OWNER` membership | ❌ (not even by itself) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ (no path exists — §3.3) |
| View Team page (active members + invitations) | ✅ | ✅ | *unspecified — see §8* | *unspecified — see §8* | *unspecified — see §8* | ✅ |
| Open workspace (any active member) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (audited) |
| Edit project metadata / publish/unpublish / archive/restore (19) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| General settings tab (21) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Screening / QA / Data-extraction / Reporting settings tabs (21) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| View project audit events / undo centre, own project (22) | ✅ | ❌ (no delegated grant mechanism designed here) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (any project) |

Rows marked "unspecified" are **not** decided by this sub-issue — they were
not among the seven questions this sub-issue's own instructions listed, and
no source states them either way. They are carried forward as an open,
low-severity gap in §8, not silently defaulted.

## 6. Creator/owner invariants, protected-member rules, membership lifecycle

- **Exactly one `PROJECT_OWNER` membership per project, always.** Created in
  the same Control DB transaction as the `Project` row itself (18 — API
  behavior), so a project is never without one and never has more than one.
- **`Project.createdByUserId` is immutable**, set once at creation, never
  accepted from the client (18, 19).
- **Structural correspondence**: the `PROJECT_OWNER` membership's `userId`
  for a given project always equals that project's `createdByUserId` — this
  is a standing invariant, not merely true at creation time, since no
  transfer path exists (§3.3).
- **Membership status enum**: `PENDING_PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, REMOVED`.
  `PENDING_PROVISIONING` applies only to the Owner's membership, only
  between project-creation and the moment the Project DB is ready **and**
  protocol `v1` is persisted (18 — API behavior); every other membership
  (added via Team, or via invitation acceptance) is created directly
  `ACTIVE` (15 — API behavior).
- **The Owner membership never reaches `REMOVED`** through any
  membership-management endpoint, by anyone, including Application
  Administrator (§3.3 — no reassignment/removal path was ever described).
  Archiving a *project* (19) is a separate, `Project`-level state change and
  does not remove the Owner's membership row.
- **Every other role's membership can reach `REMOVED` with no count floor**
  (§3.2) — a project may validly have zero Managers, zero Reviewers, etc.,
  at any time; only the Owner's presence is guaranteed.
- **Manager cannot remove or role-change the Owner** — now a redundant
  restatement of the absolute rule above, since *nobody* can, not a
  Manager-specific restriction.

## 7. Effects on future schema constraints vs. authorization/use-case logic

This decision does not implement anything (03.04/03.05's job), but it does
determine which of the rules above are database-enforceable constraints
versus application-layer (authorization/use-case) logic that 03.04/03.05
must still write in code:

**Database-enforceable (Prisma/PostgreSQL), for 03.04 to design:**
- `Membership.role` enum includes `PROJECT_OWNER` (replacing
  `PROJECT_ADMIN`), `PROJECT_MANAGER`, `REVIEWER`, `VALIDATOR`, `GUEST`.
- `Membership.status` enum includes `PENDING_PROVISIONING`, `ACTIVE`,
  `REMOVED`.
- A uniqueness constraint ensuring at most one `PROJECT_OWNER` membership
  per project (e.g., a partial unique index on `projectId` where
  `role = 'PROJECT_OWNER'`, or an equivalent 1:1 structural guarantee) —
  this is the one genuinely new DB-level constraint introduced by this
  decision; its exact mechanism is a 03.04 implementation choice, not fixed
  here.
- The existing `(projectId, userId)` active-membership uniqueness
  (unchanged from `control-database-contracts.md` §3.4).

**Not database-enforceable — must be written as authorization/use-case
logic:**
- The `PROJECT_OWNER` membership's `userId` always equals
  `Project.createdByUserId`: PostgreSQL cannot natively express "this FK's
  target equals that other table's column" as a simple constraint. 03.04
  may choose to reinforce this with a trigger, but at minimum it must be
  enforced at creation time in application code and never mutated
  afterward — this document does not choose a trigger vs. pure-application
  enforcement for 03.04.
- "Owner can never be assigned/removed/role-changed via membership
  endpoints" — the database would technically permit an `UPDATE` to that
  row; this must be a hard rejection in the membership-management use-case
  layer, not a schema-level block.
- "No Manager-count guard" — the **absence** of a rule: 03.04/03.05 must
  specifically **not** add a count-based rejection for removing the last
  Manager (an easy mistake to copy from 15's literal text without this
  decision).
- Settings/metadata tab authorization (Owner + Application Administrator
  only) — a pure API-boundary role check, not expressible as a schema
  constraint.
- `PENDING_PROVISIONING` → `ACTIVE` transition timing, gated on Project DB
  readiness **and** `v1` persistence (18) — workflow/orchestration logic.

## 8. Remaining questions and precisely what remains blocked

**Explicitly NOT resolved by this decision** (still open in
`control-database-contracts.md` §5, unaffected by anything above):

- **§5.4 — who may create a project at all** (any authenticated user vs. a
  named "creation permission"). This decision only concerns the
  representation/protection of the role *after* a project exists — it does
  not decide who may start one.
- **§5.7 — Project DB connection-mapping storage** (unrelated gap).
- **§5.9 — cross-project audit correlation mechanism** (unrelated gap).
- **§5.10 — draft-to-Project conversion disposition** (unrelated gap).
- **§5.8 — invitation-validity-period storage location** (unrelated gap).
- **22's "Project Manager... limited rights must be explicitly granted in
  the project permission matrix"** — no such delegation-granting mechanism
  is designed by this decision; Manager's audit/undo access remains flatly
  "none" until a future decision designs that mechanism.

**New, low-severity gap surfaced by this decision** (not one of the
sub-issue's seven questions, not blocking):
- Whether Reviewer/Validator/Guest may *view* (not manage) the Team page's
  member/invitation list. No source states this either way. Recorded as
  "unspecified" in §5's matrix rather than defaulted silently; 03.04/03.05
  should obtain an explicit answer or treat it conservatively
  (Owner/Manager-only) and report that choice.

**What this decision unblocks for 03.04:** the `Membership.role` and
`Membership.status` enums (§7), the Owner-per-project uniqueness
constraint, and the removal/role-change validation logic (§6) can now be
designed without guessing. **What remains blocked regardless:** anything
depending on §5.4/§5.7/§5.9/§5.10/§5.8 above, and the Team-page view-only
gap just surfaced.

## 9. Planned acceptance scenarios (NOT implemented or executed)

These are proposals for 03.04/03.05 to implement and test — nothing below
has been run, and no code exists yet to run it against.

- **Forbidden role escalation:** a Project Manager attempting to change any
  member's role to `PROJECT_OWNER` is rejected — there is no such
  assignable value from the API's perspective at all (not merely a
  permission check, since the action itself does not exist).
- **Cross-project access:** a Manager/Owner authorized in project A cannot
  add, remove, or role-change a membership row in project B by supplying
  B's `projectId` — authorization always resolves from the URL project ID,
  per the existing `control-database-contracts.md` §3.4 requirement
  (unchanged by this decision).
- **Protected-member removal/demotion:** an attempt to remove or
  role-change the `PROJECT_OWNER` membership — by the Owner themself, by a
  Manager, or by an Application Administrator — is rejected in every case,
  with no "last member" exception logic involved (there is nothing to check
  except "is this the Owner row," full stop).
- **Manager removal with zero remaining Managers:** removing the last
  active Manager in a project **succeeds** (explicitly verifying the
  rejected "require at least one Manager" alternative was not silently
  implemented anyway).
- **Provisioning failure/retry:** a failed project-creation attempt leaves
  no Owner membership transitioned to `ACTIVE` (it stays
  `PENDING_PROVISIONING` or the whole attempt is retried idempotently per
  guide 18 / `control-database-contracts.md` §3.3); a retry with the same
  idempotency key does not create a second Owner membership for the same
  project.
- **Concurrent changes threatening the Owner:** two concurrent requests — one
  attempting to remove the Owner membership, one attempting a legitimate
  Manager removal on the same project — never result in the Owner row being
  removed under any interleaving (the Owner-removal attempt must fail
  regardless of ordering, since it is an absolute rule, not a
  count-dependent race).
- **Settings/metadata authorization:** a Project Manager is rejected (403)
  from every Settings tab and every project-metadata/lifecycle endpoint; an
  Application Administrator succeeds on all of them with an audit event
  recorded.

Database-enforceable parts of the above (the Owner-per-project uniqueness
constraint, the role/status enum values themselves) are distinguished from
authorization-layer parts (the removal/role-change rejection logic, the
Settings tab checks) per §7 — a future test suite should exercise both
kinds, not assume a schema constraint alone proves the authorization rule.

## 10. Cross-reference to `control-database-contracts.md`

The following sections of [`control-database-contracts.md`](control-database-contracts.md)
now reference this decision instead of presenting the conflict as fully
open (see that file's own updated text for the exact wording):

- §3.3 (Project) — the lifecycle/lifecycle-state row.
- §3.4 (Membership) — the role enum, status enum, and last-protected-member
  rows.
- §5.1 and §5.2 — marked resolved, pointing here.
- §5.5 — the Settings/metadata half of that gate is resolved; the
  authorization-matrix-for-other-actions framing is otherwise unchanged.
- §6 and §7 — the planned-verification and handoff text updated to reflect
  the approved model instead of a still-open fork.

§5.4 (who may create a project), §5.3/§5.8 (invitation expiry), §5.6 (21's
revision-job self-contradiction), §5.7, §5.9, §5.10, §5.11, §5.12 are
**unaffected** and remain exactly as recorded there.

Clean — only the two documentation files changed, no implementation code touched.

## Report: Sub-issue 03.03 complete

**Approved decisions** (user confirmed the recommended option on all four questions via `AskUserQuestion`):

1. **Owner model:** `PROJECT_OWNER` replaces `PROJECT_ADMIN` — not a sixth role, not a derived attribute. Canonical enum: `PROJECT_OWNER, PROJECT_MANAGER, REVIEWER, VALIDATOR, GUEST`.
2. **Last-member guard:** No Manager-count floor. Only the Owner is protected, and that protection is absolute (never removable/reassignable via any membership endpoint) — not count-based.
3. **Ownership transfer:** Not supported. `createdByUserId` and the Owner membership stay permanently 1:1 bound to the creator.
4. **Settings/metadata access:** `PROJECT_OWNER` + Application Administrator only, everywhere (project metadata, all Settings tabs) — Project Manager gets none of it, overriding guide 21's self-contradicting UI-behavior text.

**Files changed:**
- **Created** `relis/docs/architecture/control-database-role-decision.md` — full decision record: status/approval, source conflicts traced to exact guide text, terminology mapping table, permission matrix, creator/owner invariants, DB-constraint-vs-authorization-logic split, rejected alternatives, remaining open questions (explicitly scoped out: §5.4/§5.7/§5.9/§5.10/§5.8, plus a newly-surfaced low-severity Team-page-visibility gap), and planned (not executed) acceptance scenarios covering role escalation, cross-project access, protected-member removal/demotion, provisioning retry, and concurrent-removal races.
- **Updated** `relis/docs/architecture/control-database-contracts.md` — §3.3/§3.4 (Membership role/status rows), §4 (ownership summary), §5.1/§5.2/§5.5 (marked RESOLVED with decision citations, original conflicting-source text preserved), §6 (planned-verification scenarios corrected to the approved model), §7 (handoff checklist, 03.03 marked complete), and the Acceptance-criteria-evidence section (updated to note the later resolution rather than leaving a stale "unresolved" claim).

**Consistency checks performed:** reread guides 13/15/16/18/19/21/22 and `PENDING-DECISIONS.md` item 2 before finalizing; traced every matrix row and invariant against its source; confirmed no remaining `PROJECT_ADMIN` reference is unlabeled (all are either historical citations or explicitly marked "renamed/resolved"); verified every relative Markdown link in both files resolves; confirmed via `git status` that only these two documentation files changed.

**Remaining blockers (explicitly not resolved here):** §5.4 (who may create a project), §5.3/§5.8 (invitation expiry value/storage), §5.6 (guide 21's revision-job self-contradiction), §5.7 (Project DB connection mapping), §5.9 (cross-project audit correlation), §5.10 (draft disposition), §5.11 (export job exceptions — already flagged, not blocking), §5.12 (audit/retention reconciliation), and the new Team-page-view-only gap.
